instruction: Attack a pin or test with injected mutants before trusting it.
outcome: An anti-gaming pin was defeated by three injected mutants: every test still passed with the defect back in the file, because the pin matched only same-line spellings. A judge caught it before ship.

instruction: Recompute; never inherit a summary or a carried artifact.
outcome: Recomputation FALSIFIED two of four carried rig artifacts; one reported a money-shaped divergence on a fleet in perfect agreement.

instruction: Write device/UI test legs as code (integration tests run by a runner script); never hand-drive by tapping coordinates or reading pixels.
outcome: ~450 calls by hand vs ~8 as tests; 128 s / ~8 tool calls vs ~11 calls per leg. Paid, but only 13 of 57 legs were convertible.

instruction: Batch device/environment testing by device STATE, grouping legs that share a state transition.
outcome: 5 state transitions for 24 graded legs: paid ~5x.

instruction: A STEP (3 min) is exactly one DAG node: one file, one behaviour, one check that proves it.
outcome: One of the five allowed dispatch shapes.

instruction: A COLLECT step (2 min) reads a finished job's log, judges it and records the verdict with its tree sha.
outcome: One of the five allowed dispatch shapes.

instruction: Run device tests only on disposable test tenants/accounts and the newest build. Never install over, write to or log into a live production tenant.
outcome: Blanket rig consent is limited to disposable tenants (directive #44).

instruction: Make every device install fresh: force-stop, clear data, uninstall, then install. Never install over an existing build.
outcome: Standing rule.

instruction: Verify the installed build with an artifact checksum and a marker-scan script, never strings | grep.
outcome: Standing rule.

instruction: Never disturb a device or environment the owner is using.
outcome: Standing rule.

instruction: Run every test root and know which roots the bare runner skips. Never delete a test root because it sits near vendored material.
outcome: Bare flutter test skips testcases/, so running only it misses 54 tests.

instruction: Reuse the shared test-data factory and an in-process database driver for DB tests instead of a private harness.
outcome: Standing testing convention.

instruction: Expose pure logic as visible-for-testing static members so it can be unit tested directly.
outcome: Pattern used by several services and screens.

instruction: Deliver to the owner only through the deliverable's gate, with a note naming every gate run (with evidence) and every gate not run. Never 'should work'.
outcome: Judged-swarm point 10 (owner, 2026-10-07).

instruction: No tunable constant (timeouts, durations, limits, retry caps) enters production code without an inline '// measured: <source, margin>' citation that resolves to a path a reader can open or a test that computes the number. A caveated citation counts as uncited. There are three outs and no fourth: (a) run instrumentation and commit the raw measurement file, (b) redesign so no constant decides correctness, (c) stop and return the constant to the architect as its own gated task. Name the out you took.
outcome: Recurrences: 1. POLICY 9a once missed 'milliseconds', so a 133,144 ms watchdog constant would have entered uncited (:166-168).

instruction: Climb verification from cheap to expensive: (1) static reality check of the diff, (2) unit suites in every test root, (3a) a login-free smoke test first, always, (3b) one batched owner-login round only if the headline needs a session, (4) the expensive battery reuses those sessions, (5) remaining owner-only checks last. Never book a login for the battery alone.
outcome: Expensive device/owner time is spent only on a build that has passed cheap checks. The battery refuses to run unless the smoke passed on the same binary.
enforcement: scripts/verify/run_battery.sh:38-46 refuses without .smoke_ok and when the APK md5 differs from the smoked md5; --skip-smoke needs a logged justification (:34-36)

instruction: Validate a guard's accept and reject patterns against the real corpus, never against one example. Before landing a check that demands or forbids a phrase, grep existing artifacts for every form they actually use. Then pin both directions: a violation blocks, and every real conforming form passes. Over-blocking is the safer failure for a REJECT pattern; under-accepting is never safe for an ACCEPT pattern.
outcome: Three instances on 2026-08-27. (1) POLICY 8 matched only 'device verification' and was silently inert on 'device battery' specs. (2) POLICY 9a omitted 'milliseconds'. (3) POLICY 9h rejected correct four-column ledgers. (1) was found only because a developer noticed its boxes matched nothing.
enforcement: none generic; the patterns live in scripts/policy_check.sh with fixtures in scripts/test_policy_check.sh

instruction: Write-enumeration law: a fix to a value in a shared record lists every writer of that collection and whether each can carry the key null or empty (across), and every money or gate key in the edited payload (down).
outcome: Promoted (REQ-047). The across axis for merge:true writes is mechanised; the down axis and other writes remain the author's job.

instruction: A wrapper that resolves its ROOT from its own path measures ITS tree, not the cwd. Invoke the target tree's own copy of the tool, or the override it names (e.g. <GATE>_ROOT), and confirm the tree it printed is the one you meant before citing its result.
outcome: The mutation battery run via main's path from a compose tree read main's yaml and refused, loud only by luck. With a yaml on both trees it would have reported green for a tree it never read. branch_health.sh gained per-gate _ROOT overrides because of this.
enforcement: scripts/verify/branch_health.sh per-gate <GATE>_ROOT override; TICK_ROOT in tick_device_box.py (cited by ledger)

instruction: Treat 'this path cannot be executed in a test' as a claim to FALSIFY. Trace the refusal path to the first dependency whose absence is fatal; a lookup inside a fail-open try/catch, or one after the return, does not block a host test. A pin that reads source or statement order is satisfied by a dead call (if (false && ...)), a flag flipped to false, or an inserted await. Name those mutations in the TDD record and show them RED; pin order and synchronicity behaviourally.
outcome: Pointer lesson (absorbs L-31). Promoted to earned working methods #5 (construct the falsifying case) and #8 (attack a pin before trusting it).
enforcement: Project instructions 'Working methods that were EARNED' #2 and #4; no script

instruction: A guard that ships unpinned cannot fail. For any diff adding a die, refusal or post-condition, DERIVE the guard list from 'git diff main...HEAD' (never from memory). Delete each guard in a scratch copy (syntax-checked) and re-run the suite. A guard whose deletion leaves the suite green is pinned or removed in the same commit.
outcome: In REQ-039, eight guards in smoke.sh, including the exit 2 refusal the acceptance criterion named, each left the 64-assertion suite at 64/0 when deleted. The rework pinned all 39 guards across three scripts with pasted REDs.
enforcement: none generic; mutation battery via scripts/verify/mutation_battery.sh

instruction: Derive a mutation table from the diff, never choose it. A hand-picked set of genuinely RED mutations still leaves the unlooked-at guards unpinned.
outcome: REQ-039's Developer had 11 real RED mutations and still missed 8 guards in the same file.
enforcement: scripts/verify/mutation_gen.py generates rows by class (exists; not opened)

instruction: Each exemption a guard carries is its own mutation: ADD an exemption and confirm something reddens. A battery naturally mutates what a guard protects and forgets what it skips.
outcome: In REQ-032, adding '--probe' to the exemption list left the suite at 25/25 GREEN, while the docs said --probe is not exempt. Code and docs were both correct, with nothing pinning them together (Recurrences: 1).

instruction: When documentation states a guard's behaviour, write a test that pins the code and that statement together, so neither can drift with every test still passing.
outcome: RIG-TOOLS.md:100 prose and .e2e_tables.mjs:1359 code agreed by accident, one edit away from being false.

instruction: A mutation whose result is a HANG is not a RED. Bound every scripted end-to-end run with a host watchdog that turns non-termination into a named failure.
outcome: A timeout die in smoke.sh was 'pinned' only by making the suite hang. After the rework, run_smoke/run_batt report '[host watchdog] killed' and FAIL.
enforcement: host watchdog in the REQ-039 test harness

instruction: Run vacuity probes on a test suite: an always-pass stub and an always-fail stub. Together they prove no assertion is vacuous in either direction before you trust the suite.
outcome: For REQ-039, always-exit-0 gave 39/25 and always-exit-1 gave 44/20. That located the defect in the unpinned guards rather than the assertions.

instruction: Reject on a proven mechanism, not a suspicion. Replay the merge and its hooks in an isolated clone, capture the violations, and show the differential against a conforming artifact at the same door.
outcome: REQ-029's Test Agent proved the shape-rule block by replay. Two sibling files matching the same regex passed because they carried a conforming line.

instruction: Mutate a guard that reads TWO sources by COLLAPSING one into the other (a = b) in each direction, not only by swapping them. Derive a fixture that puts the two sources on OPPOSITE sides of the decision threshold. If every fixture has both on the same side, the conjunct is unpinned however many mutations pass. Applies to every AND/OR over two reads, clocks, counts or stores.
outcome: In REQ-062, 44 mutations (swaps only) passed review. The judge's one-line collapse left 1909/1909 green. Shipped unpinned, it would have refused unclearable legitimate sales (a shape once reverted 128 s after merge).
enforcement: scripts/verify/mutation_gen.py class C2 emits the collapse row; the straddling fixture is manual

instruction: A transposition mutation needs a fixture that can tell the two values apart. If the fixture values are equal, change one number until they differ.
outcome: In REQ-066, swapping the Completed and Pending rows left +29 'All tests passed!' because every fixture made the two values equal. It was the third appearance of the class in that REQ. Folded into L-19.

instruction: When a rework ADDS a conjunct, the battery gains a collapse row per direction for the added conjunct. The certifier's first rung on a rework collapses the new conjunct before re-running the old findings, and the rework dispatch names the added conjunct.
outcome: In REQ-070, the 37-row battery re-ran byte-for-byte green while collapsing the new conjunct survived 39/0. A straddling fixture made the till accuse an order of colliding with itself.

instruction: Re-validate any premise about the OUTSIDE world (billing walls, CI state, fleets, vendor state, devices, indexes, counts) AT THE MERGE DOOR with the command that can falsify it. The artifact carries the command and its dated output. A card carrying a world-claim names the falsifying command; the certifier re-runs it before grading.
outcome: REQ-079 asserted CI 'has NEVER executed' and used that to skip local mirroring. 'gh run list' showed it had run SUCCESS that same morning. A REQ about a stale claim was about to ship a fresh one.

instruction: When a diff turns a silent failure into a NAMED one, enumerate the causes the SIGNAL folds together (what the API swallows), never the causes the schema declares. If the code already reads the discriminating evidence, decide the label from that read. Pin the non-headline cause with its own RED, using a fixture that produces the signal without the headline cause. A contract that names a reason states how it is derived. The tell is a comment saying 'and nothing else' or 'exhaustively' over declared constraints.
outcome: In REQ-070, INSERT OR IGNORE also swallows NOT NULL/CHECK/PK violations. On an empty terminal the toast falsely told staff 'order number unknown already belongs to a different order'. The deciding evidence was already read two lines away.

instruction: Enumerate the identifiers and strings a code region depends on, not only its branch senses, before arguing a change is safe. 'No test seam exists' is a fact about the code as written, never a law; adding a seam is usually cheap.
outcome: REQ-088 argued every failure was an over-refusal. A judge changed collection('tenants') to collection('tenant'), an under-refusal that restored the takeover with 1,957 tests, 26 battery rows, every gate and the analyzer green. The missing seam cost one method.

instruction: A battery result is not a measurement until its CONTROL is. Every committed mutation battery has a no-edit control row recorded GREEN from the SAME run, and the runner refuses to score a battery whose control is not green.
outcome: In REQ-064 the battery copied no assets, so every row died at the build step. A prior '11/11 RED' had measured nothing. It was caught only because one recorded verdict was GREEN.
enforcement: REQ-105's battery runner refuses by construction (per ledger); legacy batteries must add the row

instruction: A battery refusal (e.g. a row naming a file absent at the pinned tree sha) is not a result. Re-pin the tree to a sha carrying the rows, re-run the WHOLE battery, and record the control from that run before reading any verdict.
outcome: REQ-023c and REQ-102: reviewer-added rows made the runner exit 2; REQ-102's find strings occurred 0 times after its rework. Folded into L-24.

instruction: A merge-tree 'clean / no conflict' result is textual, not semantic. Follow every 'composes cleanly' claim with the static analyzer on the composed tree AND a run of every test file either side touches, pasted, before writing the claim down.
outcome: REQ-064 x REQ-070 was merge-tree clean and did not compile. REQ-004 x REQ-019 analyzed clean with six kitchen tests RED, since the analyzer cannot see a mock stub. REQ-092 x REQ-062 was 13/13 alone and 12/13 composed.
enforcement: scripts/verify/branch_health.sh runs gates on the merge-tree result, but runs only the branch's own tests in its own tree, so the composed-tree test run stays manual

instruction: Prove a shell check can FAIL before trusting its pass. Never use '| grep -q' under 'set -o pipefail': an early match closes the pipe, the writer dies with SIGPIPE, and 'if' reads 141 as 'no match'. Use a helper that reads to EOF (content_has) or 'grep ... >/dev/null'. When fixing one site, sweep the WHOLE file and paste the empty result.
outcome: Recurrences: 6, escalated to the repo owner. It went inert on files over 64K (REQ-066), recurred in new POLICY 12 code (5 of 17 runs, 7 of 29 battery rows corrupted), and shipped twice more in POLICY 14 within the hour.
enforcement: content_has helper at scripts/policy_check.sh:171; behavioural SIGPIPE pins in scripts/test_policy_check.sh (text scan still owed)

instruction: Treat a non-deterministic gate or test result as a race until proven otherwise: re-run the row, never average it or call it flaky.
outcome: The POLICY 12 SIGPIPE race corrupted 7 of 29 committed battery rows before anyone read it as a race rather than a flaky test.

instruction: Never put an unquoted scalar in a for-list or 'set --' (zsh does not word-split it, so it runs as ONE word). Use an explicit array "${args[@]}", a literal list, or 'while IFS= read -r'.
outcome: Three recurrences on 2026-09-08, all in verification code and all failing GREEN. A table printed STATIC on all 14 cells while measuring nothing, and a gate loop reported rc=127 as two fake gate failures.
enforcement: scripts/policy_check.sh iterates with 'while IFS= read -r'; spaced-filename cases in scripts/test_policy_check.sh (cited by ledger)

instruction: Any reset, logout or dispose path that cancels a handle (subscription, timer, stream) names the handle's re-arm site and its scope (tenant vs process) in a ledger, and pins both. A process-scoped handle must survive a tenant switch.
outcome: In REQ-094, cancelling a process-wide connectivity subscription whose only re-arm sat behind an unreset init flag froze online status after the first logout. The fix was a 13-handle ledger (scope, re-arms, cancels) pinned both ways.

instruction: Quote any command that crosses a process boundary you do not control (adb shell, ssh, sh -c, docker exec) for the far side. Its test double must reproduce the boundary (join argv, re-split, dispatch on the result), never 'case "$*"' on the command name. A double for a tool that reads stdin must also read stdin.
outcome: REQ-103's visual_check.sh had 57 green harness cases, 36 mutation rows and 0 survivors, and could not complete one real-device run because the device shell re-split the date format. adb also ate 4 of 5 surfaces from stdin while the stub reported 5.

instruction: For a script whose purpose is to touch an external device or system, one real read-only invocation of the documented call form is a mandatory cheap rung. Run it, don't read it.
outcome: Both REQ-103 defects cost one read-only real run each to find, after two clean off-device passes.

instruction: When a diff adds a REQUIRED field to a producer's output, every test double producing that output grows the field in the same commit. Check that each test passes for the reason its title names, not via a different error arm.
outcome: A fake analyser missing the new key still got its expected exit 2, but from the wrong arm. The mutation it alone killed (M-18) SURVIVED.

instruction: An ordering pin's fixture starts with the OTHER store NON-empty. Never test a restore or merge between two stores only with one store empty.
outcome: In REQ-017b every pin had memory empty at restore, so restore appending an older durable row behind newer memory survived and replayed [42.94, 0.0] again.

instruction: Define a queue's order as ONE function over the union of all its stores (memory and durable table), evaluated at drain time. Never use per-mutation-path incremental plumbing (enqueue, evict, restore, park, re-queue).
outcome: Three REQ-017b reworks fixed order one path at a time, and the fourth path broke it again.

instruction: When a guard decides on a restricted path or input set and stands down other checks, enumerate the TRIGGER SURFACE of every check it stands down. Prove each surface lies inside the decided set; otherwise the narrowing is a deviation with its own falsifying probe. A test for an acceptance clause probes the AC's scope, never the implementation's.
outcome: In REQ-125 a revert exemption was decided over 5 code dirs while the policies it disabled read the full staged set. Reverting plus an unrelated unticked fix doc exited 0, and the delivery's own test used a path inside the narrowed set.
enforcement: failure class C4 in .claude/skills/req-ladder/SKILL.md; mutation_gen.py C4 for Dart boolean guards only (shell guard probes hand-written)

instruction: A fix, pin or probe on a path with several members is not closed until EVERY member is closed. Members are exits (online/offline/bulk arms, dialog doors, error branches), navigation doors to a state, syntactic forms of a name, the arm a probe actually executes, and the receiver a fix binds to. Enumerate members by grep of dispatch, navigation and call sites, list them in the fix doc, and write one probe row per member, or declare each omission as a deviation with its own probe.
outcome: In REQ-098 the rework closed stock-erasure on one of three exits and the certifier found the other two open. A fix proven on one member narrows a defect without closing it.
enforcement: failure class C10 exit-form; scripts/verify/mutation_gen.py C2 emits one row per call site

instruction: Fix every DOOR to a state, not only the one a reviewer named. Grep every push and route; a parameter carrying null while a session is live is also a door.
outcome: In REQ-084 the Switch-Server row was fixed at the named door, while another navigation pushed login with no teardown and two screens passed currentUser null while authenticated.

instruction: Closing the qualified form of a mis-binding is not closing it. Probe every syntactic form of a name: qualified, unqualified, this., cascaded, chained, inherited.
outcome: In REQ-136 every reviewer probe used a dotted receiver. The unqualified arm on an inheriting class reproduced both original defects (a row on an untouched file, and a non-compiling row).

instruction: A probe on the non-executing arm proves nothing. A probe green on both the pre-fix and post-fix trees does not discriminate. Run probes in both directions (e.g. both timestamp orders) and name the arm that executed.
outcome: In REQ-059 a null-amount probe exercised the upload arm and was green 'for the wrong reason', while the download arm erased a settled 12.00.

instruction: Bind a self-heal or fix to the receiver the session actually uses (e.g. the per-tenant database opener), not a global handle. Verify the call chain reaches the live instance.
outcome: In REQ-107 the table self-heal ran only on the GLOBAL database, so the 'self-healing' comment and log were false on every till.

instruction: For any state derived from an async source, pin the ORDERING, not only the value. Add a fixture that folds BEFORE the source resolves and asserts the state is still correct after it does. A sticky flag set in an early fold is permanent, and a coincidentally correct value hides it.
outcome: In REQ-276 a matched printer was told 'The app has not seen this model before' on the rig. Every host probe passed because each folded with the profile already loaded.

instruction: Audit dependency-injection wiring mechanically: compute the set of consumed types over the source tree minus the set of provided types at the composition root. A non-empty difference is a crash on navigation, whatever the tests say.
outcome: The REQ-285 certifier found ReservationService and SettingsService consumed but never provided (REQ-288). Each was a screen that never opened.

instruction: A provided state object that caches a list shows its empty state forever unless something fills the cache; wiring the provider is only half the seam. Mirror the sibling's self-load and prove it with a consumer rendered over one real row.
outcome: The REQ-285 rig leg L1b FAILED beside a passing calendar view.

instruction: Produce every citation yourself by opening the file. Never inherit a citation from another agent's summary.
outcome: Recorded as 'citations produced, not inherited'.

instruction: Batch expensive device or integration test batteries instead of running them once per item.
outcome: Later scored at about 5x for batching the rig by device state (#47).

instruction: Remove dead code only after impact analysis: paste the full caller list first, then decide WIRE, DELETE or KEEP.
outcome: No measurement recorded.
enforcement: PO charter WIRE / DELETE / KEEP rule, caller list pasted first

instruction: After any deletion, run regression legs over the admin surface and the full core user cycle (in a POS, the ordering cycle).
outcome: The PO books these legs after every deletion.

instruction: After every merge that touches UI or assets, verify visually with a script that fails on blank surfaces and layout overflows. Docs-only and script-only merges are exempt.
outcome: No measurement recorded.

instruction: Keep a deterministic, delta-only test suite: fixtures, fakes and mutation batteries are committed and re-run, each requirement adds only its delta, and no reviewer rebuilds a private harness.
outcome: Delivered as REQ-105 tooling: a committed battery, a mutation YAML per requirement, a helper index and a baseline script. Saves tokens on test creation.

outcome: Every dispatch names its flows.

outcome: Purge-History was removed, with a refusal guard against its return (REQ-104).

instruction: Classify a product-code change made only of debug constructs as instrument-only, computed from the diff, and certify it without a smoke run.

instruction: No reviewer runs the full suite. Reviewers run the item's own tests, battery and gates; the full suite runs once per train on the composed tree.
outcome: Cuts repeated full-suite runs (274 in one day per #28).

outcome: Later scored at about 5x for batching by device state (#47).

outcome: Keeps #33's speed cuts from weakening testing.

outcome: Removed per-install waits on the owner.

instruction: Never pass a secret or PIN literal in a dispatch, and never guess one. Derive the value from source or config, read the attempt counter before submitting and stop within 2 of the lockout limit, and never write the derived value to a file, commit, evidence dump or report.
outcome: The PIN recorded from the owner's message was not the build's PIN. A dispatch that passed it used 3 of 5 allowed attempts, two of them by locking a test device out mid-session.

instruction: Start every device test session by waking every device and keeping the screen on.
outcome: An 'app is not running' report turned out to be two sleeping screens.

instruction: Always test on the newest composed build. A leg that passed on an older build stays valid only if the branch's code is byte-identical in the new build (check with git diff --stat old..new -- <src>); otherwise re-run it.
outcome: No device leg runs on a superseded build.

instruction: Write adversarial tests before code: commit falsification probes from the design and the failure-class list before development, have the implementer turn them green, and limit review to what the probes missed.

instruction: Every executable line a branch adds or changes must run under at least one host test, measured by coverage intersected with the diff, never asserted. Name any line no host test can reach, with its reason and the source pin that guards it.
outcome: Coverage is measured, not claimed.

instruction: Do not depend on a remote CI that cannot run. No merge waits on it, no agent re-runs or comments on its failures, and a failed remote check is not a blocker.
