instruction: Run a local CI mirror that executes the substance of every enforcing remote CI step on the exact merge-tree sha, and cite its log with that sha wherever 'CI green' is required.
outcome: Covers policy, analyze, full tests with coverage, the second test root, the 11 gates, gate tests, secret and PIN scans, and the build with a size cap.

instruction: Own done-ness: DONE means certified AND you re-read every AC against the evidence yourself. Mark each requirement's status the moment it changes: DONE with version and evidence, IN-FLIGHT with stage, or BLOCKED with the open question.
outcome: A pod's claim of done is not done-ness. Unmeasured.

instruction: Verify the whole: near completion, audit the original mandate against what shipped and commission a judge panel for the final verdict.
outcome: End-to-end outcome check, not per-card. Unmeasured.

instruction: Every deletion books regression legs covering the admin walk and the full core user cycle.
outcome: Keeps deletions from shipping untested regressions. Unmeasured.

instruction: Double review, and commission BOTH; never accept on one. The requirements owner reviews each delivery against the REQUIREMENT, AC by AC, reading the evidence personally. A judge from outside the team reviews CORRECTNESS. When they disagree, the AC named the wrong observable: fix the AC as well as the code.
outcome: CLAUDE.md notes that every blocking defect caught before a device came from a reviewer with no stake in the work.

instruction: APPROVE is incomplete until the merged build has been SEEN. On every UI/code merge, capture every surface the change could reach (screenshots attached). Docs- and script-only merges are exempt.
outcome: CLAUDE.md records a build whose restore path wedged at 0% while 1,588 tests were green, caught by one human launch.
enforcement: scripts/verify/visual_check.sh (fails on blank surfaces and overflows)

instruction: A permission sanction tied to a missing tool ends when the tool is granted. With an edit tool, fold changes in by anchor instead of rewriting.
outcome: Earned in REQ-305 spec round 4.

instruction: Before asserting a capability to an external authority (privacy policy, store listing), prove it exists in the SHIPPING artifact with a marker scan or a transitive-reachability test. A merged card proves the code exists, not that the app reaches it.
outcome: Earned in REQ-268. The reachability gate is one-hop only.

instruction: A card's DONE bar includes a mutation-battery validity check over every battery whose target files its diff touches.
outcome: Earned in CO-019.

instruction: Classify outstanding verification boxes from a pasted line-by-line grep (never a bare count), with a verdict per line and status read from the card. 'SATISFIABLE-BY-<X>' names the runner, tree sha, invocation and log path.
outcome: Earned in F-081, F-036 and F-038.

instruction: Grade each verification box against what the runner actually executes. A single-pass flow runner gives no repetition counts, second device or human judgement.
outcome: Earned in F-081, F-036 and F-038.

instruction: A failing or unrun test is not evidence of what it asserts. Run it this pass and quote the actual output, or mark it 'unverified'. An unverified figure carries no decision.
outcome: Earned in REQ-041 F-1.

instruction: Before trusting a RED control, ask 'if delivery silently fails, which row goes red?'. If none does, there is no control. Take the expected arm from an independent channel, and have every verdict row name the arm taken.
outcome: Earned in REQ-107 N-1.

instruction: Under blanket test-rig consent, wipe-install composed builds and run legs without asking per event. Ask the owner only for a login or PIN, once per wipe. Record every install (device, checksum, time).
outcome: Earned under #35: removed per-event owner gates.

instruction: Dispatch a high-risk item's verifier and judge in PARALLEL, both citing the developer's sha-stamped results. Rework only for BLOCKING findings, carrying the reviewer's committed probes.
outcome: Throughput upgrade. Unmeasured in source.

instruction: An absorbed card closes only when its invariant holds in simulation AND on the real target. Amend the card-to-invariant map as sub-cards land.
outcome: Raises rigor rather than trading it.

instruction: Every dispatch to a developer, tester or judge names the flow suites it needs, and the whole suite runs only at the merge gate. Re-deriving a committed fixture, fake or battery is grounds for REWORK.
outcome: Under #23/#24: delta-only, deterministic tests.

instruction: Verify multi-device behaviour with every change: full suite and gates after each fix, and for high-risk paths a multi-device battery where every source agrees (device A = device B = cloud). 'No errors in the log' is never evidence.
outcome: Shared working agreement 3.

instruction: After TDD and before calling work done, a judge who did not write the code reviews it against the spec AC by AC and for correctness. The verdict is APPROVE or REWORK, committed as a review file. Self-review does not count. REWORK re-enters at spec. Do not run a third full judge on a diff already judged.
outcome: Shared working agreement 12.

instruction: Run the check commands you list; never recite them.
outcome: Ties the card to executable checks.

instruction: The implementer implements the binding spec. Deviations go back to the designer, never around the designer.
outcome: Stops architecture being improvised downstream.

instruction: Run the full suite and gates after every fix. For anything touching sync, money or schema, run the two-device battery and require three sources to agree (device A = device B = cloud store). 'No errors in the log' is never evidence.
outcome: Owner directive of record (working agreement #3). Later amended in CLAUDE.md by #66: host simulation replaces the real device as a merge condition.

instruction: Gain speed without diluting checks: wait on conditions rather than sleeping, batch device commands, run independent work in parallel, and never skip a stage, a RED proof or a battery leg. Name any device scope carried over in the spec.
outcome: Owner directive of record (working agreement #6).

instruction: Read the lessons ledger before acting if it was not injected. Climb the verification ladder cheapest-first: reality check, unit tests on both roots, login-free smoke, battery, and owner effort attached to the cheapest stage that needs it.
outcome: Owner directive of record (working agreement #9, the lessons loop).

instruction: Produce citations; never inherit them. Every file:line, count and enumeration comes from a command you ran in THIS pass, cited as 'Symbol (file:NN, re-read <date>)'. A safety-bearing count pastes the command AND its output, with definition and comment hits subtracted explicitly. If you could not run the command, cite the symbol alone and write 'line not re-grounded'. A second drifted citation of the same shape is a process defect.
outcome: An unearned date stamp is a false verification claim, and an incomplete enumeration makes the argument resting on it unsound.
enforcement: scripts/pipeline/card_check.sh (BINDING [B-4] architect, [B-6] developer); prejudge citation-rot checker per CLAUDE.md

instruction: Implement the binding spec, nothing more and nothing less, one requirement at a time. Read the spec and design fully. On ambiguity, or code that contradicts the design's citations, STOP and return the question; never improvise architecture.
outcome: Keeps implementation inside the spec's boundary.

instruction: Bound a silence or timeout window by walking the emissions on the AWAITED path through each callee. Name in the spec the two consecutive sites that bracket the LONGEST span and every await between them, then double that span; never use an average. Watch for emitters only on the error path and empty progress callbacks. A measured stage duration outranks inferred continuity, and an await you cannot bound is declared as such.
outcome: REQ-030, an L-1 recurrence: a 60 s window could be shown false just by reading the file being edited.

instruction: RED first, and paste the RED. Accepted forms: run against the pre-fix source via stash, a replica then a flip, or a compile failure from a missing seam; record the form and the failure. Then the minimal fix, then green. For pure deletions, record grep-verified freedom from references and the tests that hold the behaviour.
outcome: Without a pasted RED, a test may never have been able to fail.

instruction: 'GREEN by construction' is not a RED proof. Revert the enabling hunk (e.g. git stash -p), prove the test goes red, restore, and record both. If that is impossible, declare under Deviations what the pin does NOT prove.
outcome: REQ-000-WEDGE-6 item (c) shipped a mandated item with no RED on the branch.

instruction: Run the no-disturb net after every fix and record each exit code: the analyzer (0 errors, warnings at baseline), both test roots, and every project gate.
outcome: Catches regressions outside the changed area.

instruction: Never skip or delete a test. Update a superseded pin to the new law while keeping its point. A collision with an existing test is a finding: reconcile it and document it.
outcome: Keeps coverage from eroding quietly.

instruction: End the spec doc with '## Deviations from the binding spec'. For each departure give the spec's exact words, what you did, why, and its falsifying probe. Choosing a value from a prescribed range, or reshaping a mechanism, IS a deviation. 'Deviations: none' is valid.
outcome: A '45-60 s' to 60 s choice, later falsified by the battery, had been buried in body prose.

instruction: Match the surrounding style. Comments state constraints, not narration.
outcome: Consistent codebase.

instruction: Service invariants get an assertion, never a comment: (i) cent precision, parts sum to the whole; (ii) no re-tender of a settled bill, and no partial view tendered as whole; (iii) a value leaving for a shared document is correct or ABSENT, never a placeholder null/0/[]; (iv) a failed send is retried or surfaced with the record id, never swallowed and counted as success.
outcome: Comments cannot fail. Invariants written as code can.

instruction: When you fix one site of a defect, grep the sibling sites (sibling converters, sibling paths) and fix them in the same pass.
outcome: REQ-037 and REQ-042 were the same swallowed-throw defect on sibling paths, filed weeks apart as independent discoveries. REQ-042's catch body was empty.

instruction: Mutation-prove the WIRING, not the seam. For each seam, injected parameter or dependency you add, a committed test goes RED when the PRODUCTION call site stops passing it: delete the argument in a scratch copy and paste the RED. A test that enters at the seam verifies only the seam; never report it as proving production wiring.
outcome: Both halves of an AC could be deleted with 1641+54 tests still green; the judge reproduced it with two mutations.

instruction: For a pin that gates a VALUE, write the junk value in and paste the RED. A debug accessor exposes what the collaborator RECEIVED, never a re-read of the field production reads.
outcome: Stops tautological tests that re-read their own source.

instruction: Measure a change to a signal channel (progress, heartbeat, events) in BOTH directions, and publish both inventories before reporting. What stopped feeding it: grep every producer of the old source, classify each, and tabulate worst-case silence per awaited stage before and after. What started feeding it: worst-case call count against data volume, capping or summarising any unbounded tap. Never freeze a bound as ungrounded while shrinking its input.
outcome: REQ-030: an essential sync went heartbeat-silent under a frozen window while a per-row repair loop gained an unbounded path into it.

instruction: Trace what another agent will look for. Every log line, screen state or marker a scripted check expects cites its branch condition (file:line) and the production state that satisfies it on that arm. Every contingency names its firing observation and the acceptance-bar line that judges it. Confirm the bar does not absorb or reclassify that observation; if it does, fix it now or escalate it as a BLOCKING decision.
outcome: REQ-030: a script expected a log line the timeout arm cannot emit, and the bar meant to catch a trigger absorbed it instead.

instruction: If the design and the plan disagree, STOP and say so; do not pick one.
outcome: Avoids two truths downstream.

instruction: A deviation defended by 'that case cannot exist' ships only with the falsifying fixture ATTEMPTED and its output pasted. When a probe seems to force a deviation, check the probe's fixture first.
outcome: REQ-136, 2026-09-08. This became earned method 2 in CLAUDE.md: 'construct the falsifying case; never argue it away'.

instruction: Write DELIVERED only through a branch-health script that refuses on any red gate or red own-test. The ledger entry must carry the branch tip sha and point at the green health record for THAT sha. If the branch cannot produce a green record, the step is INCOMPLETE with the red named.
outcome: Measured 2026-09-16: of 14 device-blocked branches composed for a rig window, FIVE failed their own tests or gates on their own branch. Four of the five carried a DELIVERED event stamped with main's sha. The prose rule 'full suite once at hand-off' was enforced by nothing.

instruction: Any blob or sha cited for a test run must be printed by that run's own command (run the suite, then hash the files in the same call), never carried over from an earlier run.
outcome: REQ-322 D143: a stale sha was cited for a run.

instruction: Each deviation that KEEPS an existing default or call shape owes a mutation row that flips it. Each 'never carries X' promise in your diff owes a row that appends X, or the raw exception text, to the payload. Derive both lists by grep from your own fix doc and diff.
outcome: REQ-304 side judge r2, correction 3.

instruction: Every new or moved catch clause gets a catch-narrowing mutation row (catch-all becomes a typed catch), killed by a test that throws a type OUTSIDE the expected family.
outcome: REQ-304 re-certification, judge correction.

instruction: A screen change re-runs EVERY test that renders that screen (grep every test directory for the screen class, visual and widget tests included). A DELIVERED verdict on a code tip cites both full test roots measured at THAT tip.
outcome: REQ-274: the train gate went RED with 18 failures. The branch shipped 7 visual and 1 widget case RED on its own tip.
enforcement: none (charter text); branch_health covers own files only

instruction: A GENERATED literal ships with its committed generator and a drift test.

When providing a state holder that CACHES a list, name the call that FILLS the cache before its first consumer reads it. Test the consumer over a store holding exactly ONE row, so an empty-state arm cannot pass on non-empty data.
outcome: REQ-285 re-certification REWORK: a service was provided bare and its load method had no caller, so the screen always showed empty.

instruction: Before owing a device leg on a screen, cite where every type that screen resolves from dependency injection is provided. A type that is consumed but never provided means the screen has never opened.
outcome: REQ-285 certification REWORK: the reservations screen resolved a service that nothing in the app provided.

instruction: A claim that production 'supplies X' cites EVERY producer of the value, field initialisers included. Build the falsifying fixture from that producer set before writing 'out of scope'.
outcome: REQ-285 judge REWORK: the claim missed a state field initialised to the current time.

instruction: A fixture that builds an expected string from an environment path (temp dir, home, worktree root) normalizes it the way the code under test does. Run the test once with the path ending in '/' and once without before claiming DELIVERED.
outcome: REQ-278: a test passed for the Developer and failed for the PO on the same tree because TMPDIR ended in a slash.

instruction: Async-derived state gets a fixture that checks it while the source is still null and again after it resolves. A flag's coincidentally correct default never stands in for its meaning.
outcome: REQ-276, lesson L-42.

instruction: UX rules: a refusal names the action that clears it, and a probe walks that action (no dead end behind Back or Close). A validator finding renders once. An owner-initiated cancel is never styled as an error. A progress label advances only on what it observes.
outcome: REQ-271/272 visual pass: refusals left dead ends and two red boxes appeared for one paste.

instruction: When a screen makes a dormant engine path LIVE, drive the PRODUCTION seam through the screen: each awaited call into the engine gets a catch in the same method or a real-seam test, and there is one screen-level row per value the engine can produce.
outcome: REQ-269: 19 delta rows and 7 mutations all ran a fake printer, while the real transport printer threw on a real unit type.

instruction: When a ruling names a mutant at one site, list every sibling site with the same shape (every emit branch), run the mutant at each, and paste a PASS/FAIL table. Report any survivor.
outcome: REQ-233 P1 Wave A: three consecutive REWORKs, each finding the SIBLING of what the last fix covered.

instruction: Every property that a comment, docstring or verdict string claims is a coded condition with its own dropped-half mutation row and isolating fixture, or the claim is deleted.
outcome: REQ-233 and REQ-051. Prose claims had gone unbacked by tests.

instruction: Attack a pin before trusting it: build what it would still accept and watch it pass. Pin the CALL SITE and owning file, never a declaration count or a spelling. A defect called 'unrepresentable' is actually written, with the analyzer and pin output pasted.
outcome: REQ-233 judge B-1: an anti-gaming pin caught the literal '80mm' but passed the same attack written as '80'. Another whitelisted the sanctioned constructor anywhere in the module and caught nothing.

instruction: A property over 'the files this change adds' ranges over the VCS diff name-status against the default branch, with every status letter not deliberately excluded. Never use a directory walk or a filtered slice.
outcome: Finding CO-001.

instruction: Derive a guard's escape axes from what the check actually READS, not from the last reviewer's list. Replace a source-text scan that has been defeated twice with a real parser. Every falsifier you name, you run, and you paste its output. Respelling a constant that both writer and reader use is an equivalent mutation; mutate the WRITER alone.
outcome: Finding CO-004.

instruction: A doc row that discharges a safety obligation through an existing bound cites the CALL SITE that applies the bound (timeout, guard, wrapper). If there is none, it says 'unbounded' and the residual becomes a premise with a falsifier.
outcome: CO-008: a transport bound was said to be 'supplied by' an adapter timeout, but a grep for the timeout over the new files returned nothing.

instruction: A scanner that splits its input into LINES may not claim that a whitespace pattern covers all whitespace. Pin each form's NEWLINE spelling or declare the class it under-reports.
outcome: CO-008: the scanner split lines before matching, so a call broken across lines walked past a rule written to close a one-space bypass.

instruction: A claim that a set is identical across two trees runs order-sensitive members IN ISOLATION on both trees and names which members needed it.
outcome: CO-008: a table claimed 'the same four names, identically'. The judge's own worktree produced three, because of cross-file teardown interference.

instruction: Every derived input a property row reads gets its own NON-VACUITY (non-empty) assertion, not just the input that is easy to check.
outcome: D-001-G1: a row read two derived inputs, one with three assertions and one with none, and a real modified README left the row GREEN.

instruction: When renaming or moving a code line, first grep the committed mutation batteries for the OLD text and repair both the find and the replace fields.
outcome: A rename of a notify call left a mutation yaml naming the old text, and a contract test went red on the branch.

instruction: Before fixing a path with several exits, list every exit by grepping its dispatch sites in the fix doc. Fix them all, or declare each omission as a deviation with a probe.
outcome: Lesson L-38.

instruction: Key a null-erasure guard by the set of money/gate keys, never by column nullability. Write one battery row per key, in both stamp directions.
A guard and the write it completes compare the SAME normalized form through one shared helper. Transpose the pair in the battery.
outcome: REQ-102, lesson L-17.

instruction: A decision-table change carries one mutation per CHANGED cell, plus a dropped-half row for each condition, before hand-off.
outcome: REQ-005a, lesson L-19.

instruction: When you touch a screen that a sibling branch or main widget-tests, run those test files on the composed tree and record the count.
Persist instants in UTC, parse them back as UTC, and pin the round trip under two different timezones. A comment naming an observable points at the code that reads it.
A measured figure in a code comment cites a committed fixture or test that reproduces it, or it is deleted.
outcome: REQ-123 judge F1: '1.97 s vs 0.06 s' justified routing four sites, then failed its own falsifier (0.06 vs 0.07 on two engines) and had no committed artifact.

instruction: A sort key inserted AHEAD of the ruled key is a DECLARED deviation. If its source is non-monotonic, its falsifier moves the source BACKWARDS. Every ordering fixture includes a key order that disagrees with causal order.
outcome: REQ-017b.

instruction: A guard that decides over a RESTRICTED set proves that each policy it stands down has its trigger surface inside that set; otherwise the narrowing is a deviation with a probe. Test the AC's scope. A case no row can turn red is a scope question.

Every argument of a newly wired decision, and every boolean or enum your diff adds, gets a mutation row collapsing it to a constant at each PRODUCTION call site. RUN any derivation command your fix doc states and diff its output against the row ids.
outcome: REQ-098 and REQ-086.

instruction: Probe first: committed reviewer probes run first and are never edited (report a wrong probe instead). Add failure-class rows. The coverage table maps each applicable failure class to a test id or a declared deviation.
outcome: Adversarial probes are written before code (#40).

instruction: When one predicate is split across two channels bounded by one literal cap, prove it on EVERY arm with a fixture holding a live record beyond the cap inside the capped channel's range. A comment claiming unconditional coverage names that pin.
outcome: REQ-023c.

instruction: Test a scanner or gate you write on EVERY form a member can take (async, generator, plain sync, arrow, comment-split literals, one-hop aliases). An unresolvable member is a refusal with a distinct exit code, never a silent catch-all bucket.
outcome: REQ-100: the seventh gate's resolver required 'async' and silently missed the other forms.

instruction: When a command crosses a remote shell that re-tokenizes arguments, quote for the remote. The test harness exercises the REAL argv path, never a stub of the command under test: its double joins, re-splits and dispatches on argv, and reads stdin where the real tool does. Run a changed remote hop once for real.
outcome: REQ-103, lesson L-33: the remote shell re-split arguments that the stubbed harness passed intact.

instruction: When the design REJECTS a data structure or algorithm, the battery includes a row that substitutes it back, and that row must go RED.
outcome: REQ-097: swapping Set for List in a pause lease survived all 13 Developer rows and died only to the certifier's probe.

instruction: Never pipe into 'grep -q' under pipefail; redirect grep output to /dev/null instead. Sweep sibling scripts and promote the ban to a harness scan.
outcome: REQ-079, lesson L-25: an early match closes the pipe, the writer takes SIGPIPE, the pipeline reports 141, and the 'if' reads it as NO MATCH, leaving the check inert on exactly the large inputs it exists for.
enforcement: harness scan in policy_check (promoted per charter)

instruction: Each source of nondeterminism (random, current time, uuid, clock, map order) gets a seed, freeze or reorder mutation row that must go RED.
outcome: REQ-019: seeding the order-number generator's RNG killed nothing in a 31-row battery.

instruction: Declare a mutation row EQUIVALENT only after writing the probe that would kill it and pasting that probe GREEN on the mutant. A plan sentence the code contradicts is rewritten in the same commit.
outcome: REQ-070, lesson L-15: 5 of 9 rows declared equivalent died to one probe file, and the plan described a per-refusal log that the code bounds.

instruction: Every battery carries an UNMUTATED CONTROL row recorded GREEN. A clean merge-tree is only textual, so paste the analyzer result on the composed tree before writing 'no conflict'.
outcome: REQ-064 re-merge (L-24): 11/11 REDs actually measured a missing asset bundle, and a clean merge-tree hid a 'Member not found' error.

instruction: Tests are delta-only. Reuse the shared helpers, and add any new helper to the helpers README in the same commit. Use the committed mutation battery file, never a scratch harness pasted into a reply. Run the named flow suites plus your delta, and cite the baseline script.
outcome: Directives #23 and #24: deterministic, delta-only tests and no private harnesses.

instruction: Before writing 'device-only because...', grep the test roots for the seam symbol on your branch. Any hit makes the claim false, and the pin gets written.
outcome: REQ-086 F-1: a 'device-only' claim was false because a host seam existed.

instruction: A decision over TWO sources gets a COLLAPSE mutation (set one source equal to the other at the call site, in each direction) and a swap, under a fixture that puts the sources on OPPOSITE sides of the threshold.
outcome: REQ-062 (L-19): a 29-mutation battery covered the two-source condition only by swapping. The judge's one-line collapse killed the in-memory condition and left 1909/1909 tests green.

instruction: Name each I/O boundary the diff touches together with its host fake, or write 'device-only because...'. Unimplemented contract items go under Deviations. Run the contract-vs-plan name grep first, and send any disagreement back to the designer.
outcome: REQ-012 (L-18): the whole cloud arm ran with the cloud client null in every test, mutants survived, and a contract item was omitted with no deviation line.

instruction: An analyzer claim is three counts (error, warning, info) that sum to the reported total, for the branch AND for main. A warning above main's baseline blocks hand-off.
outcome: REQ-066: a rework reported '0/0/530' while the branch carried 4 warnings of its own. The Test Agent copied the claim; the judge counted.

instruction: Derive guards to mutate from the diff (grep added lines for die/exit/return/break), delete each in a scratch copy (syntax-checked), and paste each RED. Never choose a subset; an enumeration is not a selection.
outcome: REQ-039 (L-15): deleting a guard in a smoke script left the committed 64-assertion suite at 64 passed / 0 failed. The 11-mutation table was CHOSEN rather than DERIVED.

instruction: A condition-wait waits on the same observable the downstream check READS, bounded by its timeout flag. A failure message that tells the user to set a knob the tool lacks is a false instruction.
outcome: REQ-039: a wait watched the database file size while the check 40 lines later required a populated table.

instruction: In a scripted remote command, check that interpolated values are non-empty and verify the effect by read-back or exit status. Harden sibling commands in the same pass.
outcome: REQ-039: one remote command got both checks while its sibling three lines above kept an unchecked value, a discarded rc and no read-back.

instruction: Every figure in a TDD record must reproduce from a committed artifact and be re-run after the last commit that changed the suite.
outcome: REQ-039: a fix doc stated passed=35 failed=23 (58), but no committed suite had 58 assertions. The real figures were 38/23 and later 38/26.

instruction: A mutation that HANGS is not a RED. Every scripted end-to-end runner gets a host watchdog that prints when it kills the run, and the kill counts as a failure. A pin that names a cause greps only the run's refusal lines, and the mutation is re-run to confirm it turns red.
outcome: REQ-039, lesson L-15.

instruction: A branch that can refuse, block or short-circuit a money path gets four mutation rows, each run individually: invert the boolean; delete the return/throw; swap each argument for a same-typed field; flip the enable flag. Pin any survivor in the same pass. Give an unreachable guard a testable static seam, never a pin that reads source text.
outcome: REQ-061: each of four mutations of the new tender backstop left the full 1792-test suite, all six gates and the policy check GREEN.

instruction: Test a re-armable decision with two walks. The gap walk replays, in order, every state mutation between the deferral and each re-arm. The callee walk fixes or exempts the callee's own guards.
outcome: REQ-056: a re-armed seed was unreachable on every device, because a startup call inserted a row one line after the decision and before either re-arm.

instruction: Read EVERY DDL that creates your table. If a writer emits fixed columns and swallows failure, write adaptively to the actual shape (inspect the columns) or prove the other shapes unreachable on every shipped build.
outcome: REQ-056: a metadata table had two DDLs in one file. The canonical column list failed on the second, an empty catch hid it, and the presence record silently never existed.

instruction: Before labelling a mutant 'equivalent', list every CALLER of the mutated function and the branch each reaches it from. A caller on a reachable path gets a killing host row, never a label. 'No host fixture drives it' means a missing test, not equivalence.

A NEW background poller (timer, watch, retry loop) takes the SAME foreground gate the existing pollers take. Its stop() also ends any wait AT the gate (race the wait against a stop completer). A host test backgrounds the app and asserts zero sends, then one after returning.
outcome: REQ-395 rework 1, judge F1: a poller was built without the gate.

instruction: When a fix ENABLES a control (a null handler becomes live), prove the state machine handles its event in that state. If the pair is ignored, the control is drawn inert, with a widget test that taps it and records no event, plus a control case that a live state still dispatches. A widget tap test never suppresses missed-tap warnings: scroll into view first, or the tap misses and the RED is vacuous.
outcome: REQ-397 F1: a missed tap gave a vacuous RED that also passed on the pre-fix source.

instruction: Give verification to an agent independent of the implementer, chartered to try to FAIL the delivery and to certify only when it cannot; it runs every check one by one (acceptance criteria literally, both test roots, all gates, multi-device battery on risky paths).
outcome: Standing role definition; no measurement recorded in the charter.

instruction: Run the full suite and the gates after every fix. For anything touching sync, money or schema, also run the multi-device battery with tri-source agreement (device A = device B = cloud). 'No errors in the log' is never evidence.
outcome: Working agreement 3. The basis of every battery rule below.

instruction: Gain speed without dilution: condition-waits instead of sleeps, batched device commands and parallel independent work. Never skip a stage, a RED proof or a battery leg; name carried-over device scopes in the spec.
outcome: Working agreement 6. Unmeasured.

instruction: Read the lessons ledger before acting, and climb the verification ladder cheapest-first: reality-check, unit tests on both roots, login-free smoke, battery through the wrapper. Attach owner effort to the cheapest stage that needs it.
outcome: Working agreement 9 (L-2 ladder). Unmeasured.

instruction: Produce citations, never inherit them. Every file:line, count and enumeration comes from a command you ran THIS pass (grep -n for a line, grep -rn for a set), never from an upstream spec, a report or memory. Cite as 'Symbol (file:NN, re-read <date>)'.
outcome: Working agreement 11. 'A stamped date you did not earn is a false verification claim.'

instruction: When a count or an 'all N call sites' claim carries a safety argument, paste the command AND its output and subtract definition and comment hits explicitly. If you cannot run the command, cite the symbol alone and write 'line not re-grounded'.
outcome: An incomplete enumeration makes the argument resting on it unsound, not merely imprecise. A second drifted citation of the same shape is escalated as a process defect.

instruction: Judge each acceptance criterion literally, pass/fail with evidence. An untestable criterion is a FAIL routed to the requirement owner, never waived.
outcome: Execution-order step 1. Unmeasured.

instruction: Read the spec's '## Deviations from the binding spec' section first and probe each entry against the falsifying test its author named. A spec with no such section is a FAIL back to the developer.
outcome: Execution-order step 2. Unmeasured.

instruction: Re-run the developer's new test files yourself and verify the RED proof is recorded in the spec. A fix with no observed RED is unverified by definition.
outcome: Execution-order step 2. Unmeasured.

instruction: Run every test root (not just the default one) with full counts and no skips. Any regression is a hard FAIL back to the developer, with the failing output.
outcome: Execution-order step 3. Which tree and when is governed by #28, #33 and REQ-274 (see related items).

instruction: Require every repository gate to exit 0, with baselines unmodified except documented ratchet improvements.
outcome: Execution-order step 4. Unmeasured.

instruction: For sync, money, printing or schema changes, fresh-install the build on the device rig (stop, clear data, uninstall, install, checksum-verified). For each AC with a cross-device effect, act on device A and verify the DATA on device B and in the cloud store via quiescent DB snapshots and an oracle script.
outcome: Execution-order step 5. CLAUDE.md #66 later replaced the real device as a merge condition with a host proof plus fleet simulation.

instruction: Never base a certification on an in-place reinstall (install -r is only an install-survival leg). At least one rep must wipe-install with the on-device checksum re-verified. No wipe-mode install, no CERTIFIED.
outcome: REQ-030: every install in a certified round was install -r, which the repo forbids as a verification basis (history agent-test-agent.md:412-414).

instruction: Take a smoke criterion from a rendered UI or a log probe you saw emitted, never from source. Confirm no conditional the smoke's state misses gates it, and record provenance beside 'Smoke: PASS'. A smoke FAIL whose screenshot shows the expected screen is a criterion defect: fix the criterion and re-run.
outcome: A label rendered only when a server was selected while the smoke grepped flat (smoke.sh:76) (history agent-test-agent.md:424-426). Note: later [B-3] forbids UI dumps for device legs, a tension inside the charter.

instruction: Make at least one battery leg a named real-world service scenario driven through the screens (rush, split check, item out of stock mid-order, printer unreachable, cold boot mid-order, offline then reconnect). Assert what an operator checks by eye, not row counts. A leg no real user could perform does not count.
outcome: REQ-000 was CERTIFIED on 10 cold-restore reps timing a screen with NO ORDER OPEN, which is exactly the event session-restore exists for (history agent-test-agent.md:405-411).

instruction: Measure every tunable constant in the diff against timestamped logs and report a 'Constants vs observed' table (constant, cited measurement, observed min/max/n, verdict). An unobserved constant is a residual. A falsified citation is a recurrence, with its retune requirement raised before the verdict line.
outcome: A 22-144 s envelope surfaced only because a degraded banner happened to be visible: an L-1 recurrence (history agent-test-agent.md:416-419). Constants need an inline '// measured:' citation.

instruction: Dispatch device batteries only through a wrapper that refuses to run without a green login-free smoke of the SAME build checksum. If the smoke fails, REJECT immediately without running the battery.
outcome: A stale smoke cannot cover a rebuilt APK (run_battery.sh:3-4).

instruction: After every merge touching UI code or assets, run the visual check over the reachable surfaces (at least login, dashboard, the core create flow, checkout, admin). Attach the screenshots and report per surface: rendered, blank, overflowing, or anything that looks off.
outcome: REQ-030 shipped a RenderFlex clipping. The script catches only blank surfaces and overflows (history agent-test-agent.md:129-134).

instruction: Never treat the visual-check script's exit 0 as evidence. A human or vision judgement of each screenshot is the evidence, because a rendered-but-wrong screen passes the script.
outcome: 'A rendered-but-wrong screen passes the script and fails the restaurant' (history agent-test-agent.md:134-136).

instruction: When a change removes code, walk EVERY section of the surface that held it (confirm it is gone, with no dead affordance or empty container) and every sibling section, not a sample.
outcome: A deletion's damage lands in whatever silently shared the removed import, handler or service. REQ-053's removals (five features, two screens, 224 lines) shipped with unticked device boxes (history agent-test-agent.md:144-176).

instruction: After a deletion, also run the core end-to-end transaction cycle on a real record (create, add items including modifiers, send, reopen and edit, checkout, discount, tender, close, resource frees), then confirm the same record on a second client, tri-source.
outcome: Deletion leg set B. Same incident as leg set A.

instruction: Grade deletion legs PASS/FAIL per step with the observation. A step unreachable because of the deletion is a FAIL, not a skip. A workflow already broken before the change is INCONCLUSIVE, with evidence.
outcome: Recent-changes-first cuts both ways.

instruction: Before certifying, run the spec/plan/tasks consistency analysis (one analyze process only). No tasks file, no start. A spec/plan/tasks disagreement is a finding.
outcome: 2026-09-06 owner, speckit at each stage: 'A green run with no analyze pass is not a completed stage' (history agent-test-agent.md:367).

instruction: Deliver test output as ROWS added to the committed battery plus a report, running the battery ONCE with every row (filter its output to the summary lines). A missing pin is a finding. Never rewrite the developer's runner, copy a probe into the tree or patch product code by hand. Re-deriving a committed battery is REWORK of the tester.
outcome: Owner directives #23/#24 (deterministic, delta-only tests). Unmeasured.

instruction: Probe every applicable failure class: cap/limit straddle at rank cap+1 on every arm; every argument of a new decision collapsed at every production call site; every comparator key inverted and every clock stepped backwards; every guard's trigger surface vs its decided set; every merge key nulled; every mutator's inverse; every swallowed catch; every figure re-measured. An applicable class with no probe is a finding against yourself.
outcome: Class list from PROBE-FIRST (2026-09-05). Each class traces to a judge finding (see the cap+1, collapse and equal-key items).

instruction: When dispatched before or alongside the developer, commit falsification probes from the design and the failure-class list, RED, before the fix exists. The developer turns them green, and you then certify only what the diff revealed beyond them, plus the ACs.
outcome: Owner: 'deeper and smarter, not at cost of quality'. No measurement recorded.
owner_words: deeper and smarter, not at cost of quality

instruction: For every guard whose condition names two or more sources, tabulate the existing fixtures as (source A, source B, threshold); none straddling the threshold means the guard is unpinned, which is a finding. Then add a COLLAPSE mutation (a = b) in each direction at the call site under a straddling fixture, and land that fixture as the pin. Swaps alone are not enough.
outcome: REQ-062: the certifier ran 15 mutations of its own (14 RED), all swaps. The judge's one-line collapse survived a 126-test subset and the full 1,909-test suite (history agent-test-agent.md:395-404,446-453).

instruction: A finding that redirects a device-test window must name the replacement UI entry with a file:line in the navigation code AND confirm that screen is absent from the reachability gate's unreachable-screens baseline.
outcome: REQ-063 TA-3 pointed the rig window at a screen the baseline lists as unreachable, and the architect and developer were wrongly blamed (history agent-test-agent.md:430-445).

instruction: Grade a cross-store finding, or a claim that 'the leg cannot proceed', only after grepping the other store's service and table names over the reader's file (cite each hit or withdraw) and running the recipe off-device as a host probe.
outcome: REQ-063: a HIGH finding that the editor read the wrong store missed that the screen merged both lists. The judge refuted it with a one-second widget test (history agent-test-agent.md:430-445).

instruction: With the device grant, wake and pin every test device on before the first leg (wake key, dismiss keyguard, stay-on), and record 'awake + app in focus' as row one.
outcome: Owner directive #38 (rig). Unmeasured.

instruction: Run legs behind an admin credential only on disposable test tenants, and never write the credential into a report, file or commit.
outcome: Rig rules (#38, #44).

instruction: Record every install (device, checksum, time). Use a login, never type it: carry the session around the uninstall with a session-carry script or an owner-supplied autologin file kept outside the repo.
outcome: Owner directive #44 (history agent-test-agent.md:353-366).

instruction: Derive an access code from source, never from a dispatch or speculation. Read the lockout attempt counter BEFORE the first submission, and stop and report if it is within 2 of the maximum.
outcome: Rig window 4, P4-3: the dispatch carried a code from a 3-day-old owner message that did not match the build. By the time the real one was derived the counter read 3 of 5, two attempts from locking the till out and ending the window (history agent-test-agent.md:323-335).

instruction: When a soft keyboard opens over a code dialog it shifts the layout: type on the keyboard's own numeric block, confirm the dot count in a fresh UI read, then submit.
outcome: P4-3: taps computed from a pre-keyboard dump landed on the keyboard. Note this conflicts with [B-3]'s later ban on UI dumps.

instruction: Run the committed probes FIRST and touch them LAST. A wrong probe is reported, never rewritten.
outcome: BINDING [B-1]: listed among 'the ones that cost a real defect' (card:12).

instruction: Device legs are CODE (integration tests run by a script): no coordinate taps, no UI-tree dumps, no screenshot comparison. Run the manual-taps refuser against your own plan.
outcome: BINDING [B-3]. The owner repeated it four times; the last was quoted in no_manual_taps.sh:2-3.
owner_words: we have decided to not use manual taps for testing and use innovative way of testing why this is not followed, it is non negotiable.

instruction: A probe fixture in a typed language must COMPILE. Compile or execute every fixture you author before committing the probe, and say in the report that you did.
outcome: REQ-136: probe P-C1 stood on invalid Dart. The developer loosened the generator to satisfy it, and that loosening was the hole the next review found. 'An invalid fixture pins the WRONG behaviour and the code moves to meet it' (history agent-test-agent.md:336-346).

instruction: Every battery and probe set carries an UNMUTATED GREEN control row, recorded green. An all-RED table with no control is a broken harness, not evidence.
outcome: L-24 / REQ-064: 11/11 RED rows measured a missing asset bundle, not the mutations (history agent-test-agent.md:387-392).

instruction: Before launching a mutation battery, run 'grep -cF' on each named row's edit find-string against its file in the tree the battery will run on. Launch only when every count is exactly 1; otherwise re-anchor the row or drop it.
outcome: REQ-306 TA11: the battery refused the WHOLE run at preflight on one stale find (rc=2, zero rows run) after already waiting out the suite-slot queue. Five rows had gone stale and the re-anchoring missed them (history agent-test-agent.md:289).
enforcement: none (H1 asset contract test is the whole-file form)

instruction: A cited battery, test-root or gate result holds ONLY for the tree sha it was measured at. A later product-code change voids it: re-run as a background job, or record NOT MEASURED at the tip.
outcome: REQ-274: the roots were cited at an older sha while the tip had changed the setup screen. The train found 8 RED cases (history agent-test-agent.md:291).

instruction: Make device-leg evidence survive the leg's own failure: write per-state screenshots device-side (or catch the final expect), and bound every log watcher, since the log stream outlives 'grep -m1'.
outcome: REQ-285: the failure hit the app's error override, the runner hit its 900 s alarm (rc 142) and every screenshot was lost (history agent-test-agent.md:292).

instruction: Screenshot each step BEFORE the action that leaves it, and assert the step's headline key in that frame.
outcome: REQ-273: two of seven step screenshots showed the previous step, so two steps had no visual record and the PO could not judge them (history agent-test-agent.md:293).

instruction: State whether an enumeration is closed BY CONSTRUCTION or merely UNFALSIFIED BY THIS PASS, and write the weaker sentence when it is the true one.
outcome: CO-004: three consecutive review rounds each accepted a list as closed, and each was defeated by a new member (history agent-test-agent.md:294-299).

instruction: Before accepting a guard as fixed, read its DECISION PROCEDURE and attack what it does not READ.
outcome: CO-004 round 3 found the seventh escape only by noticing a helper returned past the loop header, so a seam named in the condition was invisible to the check (history agent-test-agent.md:300-305).

instruction: Never grade a finding away as not worth fixing. One you can complete is still fixed forward in your commit: 'fixed forward' is a route, never a severity.
outcome: C10: three CO-004 items were graded 'non-blocking'. The owner promoted all three, and one was a real RFC divergence (history agent-test-agent.md:306-311).

instruction: Answer a delivery's deviation defence by CONSTRUCTING the falsifying case and, where you can, EXECUTING the reconciliation and pasting the result, rather than ruling on the argument.
outcome: REQ-136 re-certification (positive case): the pass built the fixture that broke the deviation, deleted the fallback, fixed the invalid probe and showed the set green. 'A REWORK that hands the Developer a proven path costs one round; a REWORK that hands over an objection costs three' (history agent-test-agent.md:347-352).

instruction: Treat blanket device consent as covering old-version swaps, wipe-reinstalls and the logged-in test session; none of these is a reason to return BLOCKED. A leg needing a password no agent may supply is reported to the owner as NOT-RUN with the reason, never faked or dropped.
outcome: Owner directive #44 (history agent-test-agent.md:353-366).

instruction: Before committing a probe set RED, run it against a minimal hand-written GREEN fixture that satisfies the contract, so no two probes are jointly unsatisfiable. A set passable only by a trick is a certifier defect.
outcome: REQ-136 F-1: the implementation could pass only with a trailing-TAB trick in a rows line (history agent-test-agent.md:285).

instruction: Run every erasure or overwrite probe in BOTH timestamp directions (local newer, local older), and name which arm executed the code under test.
outcome: REQ-059 TA-2: a null-erasure probe with the local row newer exercised the upload arm, where the projection never runs, so the value 'survived' because nothing ran (history agent-test-agent.md:262).

instruction: Give every ordering test row a sibling with EQUAL keys and a stated winner. Transposing distinct keys proves direction, not tiebreak.
outcome: REQ-017b F6: two envelopes with equal enqueue timestamps replayed stale-last (history agent-test-agent.md:268).

instruction: Read a test pin before citing it, and state in your own words what it compares.
outcome: REQ-059 J3-2: a report cited a test as pinning set equality with a scanner, but it compared fixture keys to the set and never touched the scanner (history agent-test-agent.md:270).

instruction: For EVERY capped channel, one fixture seeds cap+1 records in the channel's own range with the target at rank cap+1, on EVERY arm the cap applies to. Cite it by id per cap, or the certification is incomplete.
outcome: REQ-023c J3-B1, a recurrence escalated to the owner: the straddle rule was in force, yet the named probe twin seeded 40 docs against a 900 cap (history agent-test-agent.md:274).

instruction: Before any device leg, prove the installed build is the NEWEST composed one (the on-device package checksum equals the recorded one). Carry an older PASS forward only with an empty 'git diff --stat <old tip>..<tip> -- <product code>'.
outcome: Owner directive #39 (history agent-test-agent.md:278).

instruction: A clean 'git merge-tree' is only TEXTUAL: run the analyzer/compiler on the composed tree and paste it before writing 'no conflict'.
outcome: L-24 / REQ-064: a clean merge-tree hid a 'Member not found' compile error (history agent-test-agent.md:387-392).

instruction: Run the committed mutation battery and paste its table. Add your mutations as rows in the same file, never a private harness. Reuse and index the shared test fakes, and run the flow suites the dispatch names.
outcome: Owner directives #23/#24.

instruction: Run the repo's check commands (baseline, suite slot, committed battery, dispatch check, can-finish, task-DAG order, card check) rather than reciting them.
outcome: Card check-command block. Unmeasured.

instruction: A step is DONE when its check passes, not when its agent says so or the work feels finished. Re-run the check yourself in the verify step. A claim with no executable check is not a result.
outcome: Orchestrator BINDING [B-1].

instruction: Ground every claim in file:line or an evidence path, and re-measure every figure with the command that produced it. A number you cannot reproduce is a claim, not a fact.
outcome: Operating method 4 (L-1).

instruction: Adversarially self-review before declaring anything: ask what was not tested, what a skeptic would try and which sibling site a grep would find, and run that check now in the same step rather than noting it.
outcome: Operating method 5 (L-10).

instruction: After each stage run a verify step: re-execute every step's check, confirm the outputs exist, the probes are GREEN and unedited, sha-stamped results are cited and the context file is complete, and for a delivery read the ACs literally against the evidence. Verdict: DONE, or BLOCKED with the exact failing check.
outcome: Duty 3 (verify the product). Unmeasured.

instruction: Verify a claim with a probe that can DISCRIMINATE (it would fail if the defect were present), and say 'inconclusive' rather than banking a green.
outcome: Two attempts at a poll-loop escape were worthless: one was confounded by an unrelated rule, one too degenerate to be in scope. 'Recording its green is worse than recording no result.'

instruction: Let evidence choose which members of a class to fix. Never bulk-edit the whole candidate set blind.
outcome: Of 241 unflexed Rows, about 17 actually overflowed. Editing all 241 would have been a guess big enough to create a new defect class.

instruction: Prove every fix RED first and paste the Expected/Actual output.
outcome: The skill's rationale: 'A fix without an observed RED proves nothing.'
enforcement: probe commit convention 'test(<REQ>): probe-first — <n> probes RED'

instruction: Pair every RED proof with a GREEN control that would tell a correct build apart from a degenerate one.
outcome: L-24: without an untouched-order-stays-pending control, the close and cancel tests would both pass on a build where every order reads back completed.

instruction: Make every guard fail on purpose before you rely on it.
outcome: Nine guards in the repo read correctly and did nothing.

instruction: Do not ask a code graph which tests cover a file when it has no test-to-source edges. Use an import-based affected-tests tool and say the graph cannot answer.
outcome: The graph had zero test/ to lib/ import edges.

instruction: Device and UI verification legs are code: integration tests run by a script. Never hand-drive taps, UI dumps or screenshot comparisons as the thing you observe.
outcome: Hand-driving cost ~450 tool calls for ~40 legs. The same work as tests cost ~8 calls in 128 seconds.

instruction: Make test builds sign themselves in on disposable accounts using build-time defines from a file kept outside the repo. An authenticated session is not a reason to ask the owner.
outcome: Device legs became hands-free once the owner supplied the autologin file (REQ-117).

instruction: Never touch the owner's in-use device or emulator; keep it under a lock agents respect.
outcome: Pods once force-stopped and wipe-installed the app under the owner mid-use. That was the reported 'the app crashed'.

instruction: Check layouts on every form factor (phone and tablet), not just one, before merging UI.
outcome: The visual gate ran on a tablet only, though two of three tills are phones. No merge had ever checked a phone layout, and 17 RenderFlex overflows shipped.

instruction: After every merge that touches UI, run a post-merge smoke that drives the main flows on every device and fails on any overflow.
outcome: Added after the 17 shipped overflows.

instruction: Before believing any check, gate, guard, report or board, run it and try to break it. Never trust a verdict from reading the tool's code.
outcome: Eight instruments in the repo were found silently wrong in one day. None was caught by reading; every one was caught by running it.

instruction: Make sure a multi-party test harness passes every coordination parameter. A test that can only ever fail is a defect in the instrument.
outcome: legs.sh passed no rendezvous defines, so two-till legs could only ever fail.

instruction: Check that every mutation row's find-pattern actually matches the source before trusting its kill.
outcome: Eight mutation-battery rows had a find string matching nothing and reported kills they never attempted.

instruction: Prove a guard in both directions: the input that should be refused is refused, and the one that should pass is permitted.
outcome: From the skill: 'If you cannot make a guard go red, you have not got a guard — you have a passing message.'

instruction: Ask what a check actually opens, and whether that is the artifact production or the test rig really produces.
outcome: marker_scan.sh opened lib/arm64-v8a/libapp.so, which the debug APK every leg installs does not contain.

instruction: Check every path a script tests against where the file is really written (e.g. $HOME vs repo-relative).
outcome: can_finish.sh looked repo-relative for a file deliberately kept in $HOME, falsely owner-blocking 20 cards. After the fix: BLOCKED 20 -> 0. A one-second ls would have caught it.

instruction: Capture an exit code from the unpiped command, immediately. 'cmd | head; echo $?' reports head's status.
outcome: Reading rc=0 through a pipe nearly filed a false 'inert guard' finding. Unpiped, rc=2 and the guard was failing loudly and correctly.

instruction: When a verification reports a miss, check the verifier before filing a regression. A check stricter than the truth manufactures defects.
outcome: A precision check scored 24/25. The 'miss' was Tween<double>(, a real call the checker's regex rejected; the extractor was right and the verification wrong.

instruction: Never write 'grep -c ... || echo 0'. Use '|| true', then strip to digits with tr -dc '0-9'.
outcome: grep prints 0 and exits 1, giving '0\n0'. '[' aborted, the test took its permissive branch, and the load guard never fired.

instruction: Count analyzer/linter severities with ^[[:space:]]* (never ^\s+) and confirm they sum to the tool's 'N issues found' line.
outcome: Warning lines are not indented and were read as zero.

instruction: Key exemptions and allow-lists on trimmed source text, never on line numbers.
outcome: Every insertion above a line-keyed exemption produced a false RED; this was paid four times.

instruction: Measure a new guard's blast radius against existing artifacts before merging it.
outcome: POLICY 17 was checked against 132 existing fix docs (7 would trip) before landing, so it did not break every future merge.

instruction: Name in every dispatch the flow suites a requirement touches (ordering, checkout, sync, login, printing, ...) and run those plus the delta while working.
outcome: Tests are delta-only (#23/#24).

instruction: Failure class C1: probe cap/limit straddles. Seed cap+1 records inside the channel's own range, target rank cap+1, on EVERY arm the cap applies to.
outcome: Each class on the list cost a REWORK. Taught by REQ-023c J3-B1.

instruction: Failure class C2: for each new decision, replace each argument with a constant at every PRODUCTION call site and confirm a test goes red.
outcome: Taught by REQ-098 TA-1/2.

instruction: Failure class C3: never derive an ordering key from a non-monotonic source. Probe with the clock stepped backwards and a restart between two enqueues of one entity.
outcome: Taught by REQ-017b TA3-F10.

instruction: Failure class C4: a guard must be at least as wide as the policies it switches off. Enumerate each disabled policy's trigger surface and test a fixture OUTSIDE the decided set.
outcome: Taught by REQ-125 AC2.

instruction: Failure class C5: for every partial-merge write, null or omit each payload key while a peer holds a value, and assert money/gate keys survive (the DOWN axis).
outcome: Taught by REQ-043/044/098 F3b.
enforcement: merge_key_gate.sh covers only the across axis (per CLAUDE.md); otherwise probes

instruction: Failure class C6: every mutator has an inverse that reaches the same chokepoint (delete -> tombstone).
outcome: Taught by REQ-020/104.

instruction: Failure class C7: make each catch swallow, and assert the error is REPORTED, not just logged.
outcome: Taught by REQ-093/107.

instruction: Failure class C8: re-measure every figure in code or docs with the command that produced it.
outcome: Taught by L-1 and REQ-126 F3.

instruction: Failure class C9: pin the test clock in UTC and pass it through to the callee. Probe for DateTime.now() inside a callee under a pinned test.
outcome: Taught by REQ-020 F-J2-1.

instruction: Failure class C10: run the sibling-site grep the developer did not, over every writer/reader of the owning collection (the ACROSS axis).
outcome: Taught by L-10 and REQ-043.

instruction: End every stage with a verify step. It re-runs each step's check, confirms outputs exist, confirms probes are green and unedited, confirms sha-stamped results are cited and the context file has a section per step, and reads each AC literally against the evidence.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Probe first. Before any fix exists, a certifier writes and commits falsification probes: one per acceptance criterion as an observable and one per applicable failure class. Each is RED on the current tree with Expected/Actual quoted, compiles, and uses only committed test helpers.
outcome: Owner directive #40. Moves review effort before the code.

instruction: The developer turns every committed probe GREEN without editing any probe. A wrong probe is reported, never rewritten.
outcome: Keeps the tests independent of the implementer.

instruction: The developer adds tests for what the probes missed, by failure class.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Run the mutation battery once per delivery with a green CONTROL and judge every survivor. Generated survivors are delivery failures unless marked equivalent.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Compare analyzer counts to a recorded baseline and run every gate individually with its rc. Skip a gate only with a stated reason, and only for changes confined to docs/scripts.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: The certifier certifies by execution what the probes did not anticipate: every AC literally, probes green and unedited, diff-revealed failure classes (writing any missing probe now), no deleted or skipped test, and its own sibling-site grep.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: A train for a card that owes device legs merges only when every owed leg has a PASS row on the newest build. Otherwise it returns BLOCKED naming the legs.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: The developer works on a feature branch off main, RED-first. Developer questions go to the architect, never around them.
outcome: No measurement given.
enforcement: POLICY 11 blocks direct commits to main

instruction: The tester executes every criterion, suite and gate one by one. REJECTED goes back to the named owner and is re-tested; CERTIFIED continues.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Verify distributed sync from DATA agreeing in every replica (device A = device B = cloud) for anything touching sync, money or schema. 'No errors in the log' is never evidence.
outcome: Working agreement #3.

instruction: Climb a cheapest-first verification ladder: reality check -> unit tests in both roots -> login-free smoke -> battery via the sanctioned runner -> owner effort only at the cheapest stage that needs it.
outcome: L-2 ladder.

instruction: Hold the device rig under an exclusive lock. The battery runner refuses without a holder and a free lock; never bypass it with a skip flag. A team blocked on the rig takes a non-device task.
outcome: Two concurrent batteries corrupt both (force-stops mid-rep, wiped sessions, a third writer). 'A corrupted battery that still prints numbers is worse than no battery.'

instruction: Batch device batteries. One run certifies every merged fix whose legs it covers: union and dedupe the legs, grade each item on its own ACs, and split only when legs interfere, saying why.
outcome: One battery measured 5,670 s; 17 MUSTs run serially would be 25-30 h of device time.

instruction: Batching never lowers the bar. Every leg each AC demands still runs, and an observable that cannot tell success from not-run is refused.
outcome: Rules L-7 and AM-1.

instruction: Classify a diff as INSTRUMENT-ONLY by script when every line is an assert, debug guard, test seam, comment, import or bracket. It certifies without a device smoke; claiming the class over a production line fails the commit.
outcome: REQ-110's fifteen debug lines had cost two release builds and forty certifier turns.

instruction: Guard at the point of expense. A cheap smoke records the artifact checksum and criterion; the expensive battery refuses unless the smoke is green for the exact checksum about to be installed. The skip flag must be justified in the run log.
outcome: Earned by the 5/5-failing build described in the dispatch-preflight item below.

instruction: Speed removes waste, never rigor. Every branch keeps the RED-first proof, the committed battery with its control, both test roots on every train, all gates, and a real-environment leg for sync/money/printing/schema.
outcome: Owner directive #34. CLAUDE.md #66 later lets a host simulation replace the device as the merge condition.

instruction: Always install fresh on test devices (stop, clear data, uninstall, install; never install-over), and record every install (device, checksum, time).
outcome: Owner directive #35.

instruction: Never type a credential or PIN, never touch the live production account, and test only on disposable accounts.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Route every in-repo test caller through the wrapper, and keep a test that fails on any bare test invocation under scripts/, so a bypass is caught by a test rather than an incident.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Wake test devices and pin the screen on at the start of every device session.
outcome: Asleep screens read as 'the app is not running'.

instruction: Test only on the newest build composed from the merge-ready set. Carry a PASS forward from an older build only for a branch whose code is byte-identical in the new build.
outcome: Owner directives #39 and #44.

instruction: Use the login, never type it: carry the session across fresh installs or self-login from an owner-supplied gitignored file. A leg blocked on a password no agent may supply is reported NOT-RUN, never faked or silently skipped.

instruction: Implement in the validator's printed topological order, least-dependency first.

instruction: Resolve each dependency by implementing and verifying it before its dependents. Never assume it already holds.
outcome: The skill's warning: 'A will probably be fine' is how a dependency-ordered list becomes wrong silently.

instruction: Never skip ahead to a node whose predecessors are incomplete. If an edge looks wrong, stop and report it as a DAG finding.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: If the DAG validator fails, do not implement; fix the DAG first.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Run tests only through the repo's test wrapper (which holds a machine-wide slot lock), and only on named files. Never run the bare test runner.
outcome: Caps concurrent suite runs on the machine (two slots).

instruction: No duplicate code: extend the nearest existing code and test helpers, and name the reuse targets in the dispatch prompt.
