instruction: Have the Developer fix ONLY the listed path gaps, in order, each RED first: a failing test that shows the gap, then the smallest fix, then green. Touch only the files each gap names, and run only the affected tests.
outcome: Keeps fix steps narrow and TDD-proven.

instruction: Prove the outcome with ONE end-to-end test that walks the whole path on the repo's fakes. Reuse existing rigs and fakes by importing or extending them, never copying. Add the isolation, safety and performance assertions from the evaluation file that a host test can make.
outcome: A single proof of the outcome replaces per-task certification.

instruction: A defect in the test agent's own test or fixture is the test agent's to fix, never the product's.
outcome: Earned by D160: a lane looped for 3+ hours on harness items sent back to the developer.

instruction: Report every mutant run with expect RED: it must fail. A mutant that passes (survives) is a hole in the proof and counts as an open item.
outcome: Earned in REQ-306 round 3. A kill is the proof working; a survivor blocks the judge.

instruction: Work the backlog with one Developer per lane, ONE TASK AT A TIME, TDD, in the order the DAG validator prints.
outcome: Comes from the owner's instruction on task order.
owner_words: complete all tasks in logical order and then llm as judge review test and fix issues; take one task use tdd and implement one by one; finish first all tasks quickly

instruction: For each task, read only its line and the code it names. Treat an automated PRESENT/PARTIAL/ABSENT existence check as a hint, never as proof.
outcome: Evidence of code is not proof it works. An earlier swarm left work done but unticked.

instruction: Count an already-built task as done only after running its test and seeing it green.
outcome: Stops unverified ticks.

instruction: A RED test must fail for the reason the task states. A compile error in an unrelated file is not that reason.
outcome: Stops false RED proofs.

instruction: For an implementation task, make the smallest change that turns its RED test green.
outcome: Minimal TDD fixes.

instruction: Run dependency tests once per step, after the last task: compute the tests of every module that imports what you changed (affected-tests script) and run them all through the suite wrapper. A failure there is yours to fix before you return. The same applies after judge fixes.
outcome: Comes from the owner's instruction on dependency testing.
owner_words: keep doing dependency testing with other modules in sequence

instruction: Never mark a device leg, real-cloud run, console or deploy step, or anything owner-only as done in an agent step. List it as skipped with the reason.
outcome: Skipped items are passed to the judge (task-by-task.js:83).

instruction: Prejudge step contract: run the checker script with at most 3 tool calls. Turn each FAIL line into one fix whose change is that check's detail lines verbatim and whose why names the check, targeted at the lane that owns the files (or 'all'). Fix nothing and read nothing else. Skip side tracks, since their own swarm checks them.
outcome: Mechanical failures are routed to producers without spending a judge.

instruction: Split verification into LAUNCH and COLLECT. The launch step starts long checks in the background and returns INCOMPLETE with each log and pid. A separate later collect step reads the logs and alone gives the verdict. A job still running after the allowed collects is UNVERIFIED, which no gate may read as a pass.
outcome: Implements #48: a step never waits on its own job.

instruction: In a launch step, write each mutant as a row in the mutation yaml and never mutate a source file in place while a job runs. Run the battery only for your own lane's rows, never the whole file. Start every long job with nohup, with its log under the scratch verify dir and its pid recorded, then return INCOMPLETE at once without sleeping, polling or tailing.
outcome: A kill set red elsewhere in the shared tree must not refuse your lane's rows.

instruction: In a collect step, check each job by pid AND log (pids recycle, so a pid alone is not an identity). If any job is alive, return PENDING with every running job, including new pids of chained stages. Never start, restart or wait on a job. If a job ended without a usable result (died, refused, ran no rows), return RELAUNCH with the reason. Otherwise read each log, judge it with its tree sha and return DONE.
outcome: Earned on 2026-10-07: collects restarted batteries the waiter could not see and answered PENDING ten times.

instruction: A lane developer edits ONLY its owned files and executes only its DAG nodes in topological order, RED first and shown. After each node it appends one ctx Log line (node id, file, check result) and skips nodes the Log already marks done. Needs outside its ownership go under 'Cross-lane requests' and the lane continues.
outcome: Resumable, conflict-free lane work.

instruction: A lane finishes by running the analyzer on its files, its tests via the suite wrapper, every gate its files can affect, and the golden/preview diff when there is an approved design. It leaves device-verification boxes unticked and returns the activity-log entry text.
outcome: Lane delivery is self-checked before verification.

instruction: Verify each lane in its OWN tree (HEAD plus only that lane's uncommitted files), never on the shared working tree. Run its tests, analyzer and mutation battery from inside it.
outcome: On 2026-10-07 every battery of the relaunch ran zero rows on the shared tree: BASELINE-RED from another lane's half-done code, a row whose target another lane had moved, and a scratch held by another REQ's live battery.

instruction: The adversarial test agent first runs the prejudge checks and cites every FAIL in the lane's files as blocking. It runs only the affected tests (the full suite runs once per batch at the train), generates mutation rows by failure class before the battery, injects at least 3 mutants against the lane's most important behaviour, and checks the lane against its ACs, evaluation rows, the honesty rule, the repo rules and duplication.
outcome: Adversarial certification per lane.

instruction: REWORK only for product defects. Defects in your own probes, fixtures, harness or battery rows are yours to fix in the next launch and are never sent to the developer. A red CONTROL means the probe is wrong, not the product.
outcome: D160: a lane looped for 3+ hours on harness items.

instruction: Accept only when PO acceptance APPROVEs AND the final judge PASSes, looped. The PO judges against the spec, compares every golden with its reference (both images) via the preview diff, rates each scene exact/close/off/missing with concrete diffs and the owning lane, and lists only blocking items. The final judge (after a final prejudge) checks spec-to-code traceability, every evaluation row, honesty of every screen, repo law, token use across the run and owner-only items. Rework is routed to the owning lanes.
outcome: Implements the double review: PO 'does it satisfy the requirement' plus judge 'is it correct'.

instruction: A re-gate's passing-test count must be at least the previous tip's count with 0 failing and 0 skipped. A lower count means a test was deleted or skipped: name every missing test before merging.
outcome: The rework branch showed 6677 passing against the train tip's 6768, i.e. 91 missing tests, caught as a merge check.

instruction: A mechanical check with a record of false positives is not a merge blocker. A human or vision pass judges its output.
outcome: visual_check BLANK false-positived four times on Flutter surfaces.

instruction: Turn a quality sweep into a ratchet as code. Tests print violations=N for the mechanical half of the bar, the counts are committed and may only fall, and fixes drop them to 0. The judgement half is one vision pass with at most 5 findings per surface, each citing a frame and a rule.
outcome: 'A sweep that produces opinions produces rework rounds; a sweep that produces a ratchet produces merges.'

instruction: Check that a grep-based finding matched the right thing (file path vs class name) before calling something a hallucination. Withdraw the finding when it did not.
outcome: D51's 'hallucination' finding was withdrawn: the grep had matched a same-named class in a different file.

instruction: Do not demand a result the current environment cannot produce (e.g. pins to commits a shallow clone lacks). Score by a stated mechanical rule and owe the literal green run in the full clone before merge, so no gate is weakened.
outcome: 'Demanding a green this clone cannot produce is a bar the team cannot see.'

instruction: Certify the NEWEST commit that touches the deliverable's paths, never the first add of a file. A path-limited 'git log --diff-filter=A' returns the add commit forever.
outcome: A rework round would otherwise re-score a stale tree. A certify score on an older sha is void.
enforcement: certify step reads the orchestrator's commit record (D61)

instruction: A re-implementation of an existing builder or helper is a REVISE (no duplicate code). Fix it at the root by importing the single public builder.
outcome: A duplicated FleetStateView builder in a test was replaced by one public fleetStateView used by both callers.

instruction: Grade a mutation row the compiler refuses as KILLED-BY-TYPE-SYSTEM, not as a survivor.
outcome: Two null-promotion inversions could never build, so they count as kills.

instruction: A lane verifier whose diff touches a hub file runs the lane suite plus the tests that name a symbol its diff changed. The importer-wide run is the batch suite, run once on the combined tree before any push. No lane is merge-ready before that batch suite is green.
outcome: Measured: 8 lane files took 2 min 49 s of slot time after a 23 min queue. Per-lane importer runs were three near-full suites on uncombined trees that the batch repeats anyway.
enforcement: none recorded (overturn: batch suite fails an importer the symbol set missed)

instruction: A probe set whose control arm is red is not evidence. Delete it and re-add it only with a green control.
outcome: A committed probe failed in its CONTROL arm and was ordered deleted.

instruction: Pin generated mutation rows by content, never by positional generated ids.
outcome: Positional ids shifted and blocked a lane on harness work.

instruction: When many visual comparisons fail at once, find and fix the few product differences that shift everything first. Then list any remaining failures one by one with their diff, never as a lump.
outcome: 52 'off' scenes were explained by two differences (a two-line header causing an 8 px shift, and headline copy).

instruction: 'Proven' means proven on the real system. A green host proof is a step, not the proof. (Later amended: an exhaustive simulated-environment proof replaces the real device.)
outcome: The machine had no SDK, emulator or credentials, so the real-system leg was batched for the owner. This was superseded by D321.

instruction: A gate whose inputs are absent from the tree is recorded NOT APPLICABLE, proven mechanically with the sha, and never recorded as a PASS or a waiver. The gate list is the one the tree's own instruction file names.
outcome: An 11th gate absent from main would have measured another REQ's files, not this one.
enforcement: git diff --name-only proof recorded with sha

instruction: A ratchet baseline edit inside a merge may only shrink. Any increase is a REVISE.
outcome: Silent-noop catches went 117 to 113 and 103 to 102 on the cut, allowed as shrink-only.

instruction: Replace the real-device leg with a simulated-environment proof. (a) A deterministic fleet simulation: two or more clients share one fake backend, each with its own local store; every pass kind runs; assert convergence on every client, reads that scale with changes and not data age, and fault scenarios (offline, quota latch, cache-only, restart mid-pass, refused write). (b) Diff coverage measured mechanically: coverage intersected with the diff, never asserted; an unreachable line is named with its reason and guarding pin. (c) Every guard killed by a mutant (0 unexplained survivors, 0 invalid), and every new test proven by a mutation row that turns it RED. State the limits: real backend semantics stay covered by source pins.
outcome: REQ-306 merged without a rig. Diff coverage on the cut was 775/776 (1 waived) and the final judge panel PASSED O1-O7 (D334/D335).
owner_words: Ignore real device test and ensure each for Is tested with stubbed data and simulated environment or data, this should ensure each and every code is crystal clear quality

instruction: A diff-coverage waiver is only for a line that cannot execute, never for a broken one. It is one per-line row with the reason plus the source pin and mutation row that guard it. A whole-file waiver over an executable change is refused. A waiver that becomes hit or stale fails the check, so it retires itself.
outcome: One waiver (a session-end-mid-upload arm) stood on the cut. Two dead legacy labels were waived per line, with the waiver rows deleted when the dead code goes.

instruction: Never pin a fixture date that production code compares against the real clock. Derive the fixture epoch from the run's real date.
outcome: With the fixed epoch, simulation rows would have fallen outside the 7-day active window after a week (F-CLOCK). The harness was fixed.

instruction: When remote CI cannot run (no runners), local CI on the same head sha is the CI of record and the PR body says so. Never wait on, re-run or count the broken remote checks.
outcome: GitHub Actions jobs ended in ~2 s with no logs. Failures on branch and main alike were not counted.

instruction: Code from a lost or old branch is evidence, not a patch to cherry-pick blind. Re-implement it on current main, RED first, as its own outcome-first run.
outcome: 116 tags were not ancestors of main. The recovery train was rebuilt per outcome.

instruction: Outcome-first runs call the mechanical pre-judge checkers before the outcome judge.
outcome: No pre-judge report existed for an outcome-first run, so the run had no mechanical pass.

instruction: Before a GO on any copy change or revert, grep every distinctive fragment of the old and new sentence in the test and mutation directories, open each hit, and run the mutation-file check on every battery whose find touches the changed file. A hit attributed without opening it is a miss.
outcome: Two judge rounds missed a test pin and orphaned mutation rows that the PR review bot found.

instruction: A text-change dependency check greps the mutation files for a distinctive substring, never the whole line, because mutation strings are escaped.
outcome: An earlier 'no dependency' grep missed the mutation yaml.

instruction: Local CI tolerates exactly a committed known-failure list, so one run reaches every test root. The list only ratchets down, and growing it needs a recorded decision. RED control fixtures cover over-the-list, no-summary and exact-set. The final line never prints a silent green. Measure before and after, and revert if it does not pay.
outcome: Three trains each recorded 'ci_local failed at stage test, 72 on the list, 0 beyond', then hand-joined known_failures.py and a separate testcases run. A gate that can never pass gets routed around by hand.

instruction: A guard that cannot be shown going red is not trusted. Every guard, gate or bar ships with a control that turns it RED.
outcome: No control existed for the known-failure filter. Every new perf bar needs a mutation row proving it can go RED.

instruction: A guard bar must never penalize removing duplicate code. When a line-count check trips on a dedup, amend it to destination-preserving rules pinned by tests instead of forcing the duplicate back.
outcome: A navigation line-count bar flagged 12 lines removed by a word-for-word duplicate's removal. The bar was amended.
enforcement: amended B-2 bar with per-class pinned tests

instruction: Fix a shared instrument or base file once, on the integration base, by its single writer, then have every lane sync it. Never grade with a gate red.
outcome: A harness crash was inherited by every lane, and one base commit repairs it for all. Lane-local edits to a shared rig were re-conflicted at every sync.

instruction: Performance bars: use a deterministic in-test count bar (rebuilds, elements, render objects at most base x1.10) plus a coarse timing ceiling (x2.0). The fine timing bar comes only from an alternating base/head compare in one job (5 or more rounds, median of medians). Never wait for a quiet slot. RED is never waived.
outcome: The single-run x1.10 in-test timing bar (D983) was superseded: rounds spread 20-80% under load, so a 10% bar was a coin flip. Counts are exact.

instruction: Attribute a performance excess with per-component revert arms before any rework, against a pre-registered outcome table. Never remove a graded visual to buy budget. Record baselines only on WITHIN BUDGET, by the record procedure, never hand-typed.
outcome: A x1.44 excess tracked render-count ratios, so it was structural, not noise. The arm method then found the app bar to be the cost (D1231).

instruction: Evidence proves only the tree sha it ran on. The merge gate needs a run on the final tree sha, and a run on an earlier sha counts neither for nor against the head.
outcome: A ci_local run on 25eb77076 did not prove head 796b61ec3.
enforcement: verdicts recorded with tree sha (COLLECT shape)

instruction: Capture a script's own exit code before piping its output through tail (set -o pipefail).
outcome: A diff-coverage RC recorded tail's exit code, not the script's.

instruction: A test must drive the call path shipped code actually uses. A test of a path with no production caller proves nothing.
outcome: Staff-PIN rows called an auth method with no lib/ caller: REVISE.

instruction: One shared helper serves every field that needs the same normalisation, never one copy per field.
outcome: One whole-number helper serves hour, minute and partySize.

instruction: Read-only analysis is not a mutation kill, and a test's kill list is a prediction until a battery runs it. Measure before passing.
outcome: G1-G9 edits had zero runs on the tree. REVISE until the battery was measured.

instruction: A change that adds a silent catch must log instead (the error type only, never the message, which may echo a secret) before delivery. Update the gate baselines of improved files in the same commit.
outcome: The silent-noop gate went red 5 to 6 on the diff's one new catch.

instruction: Run every test invocation through the repo's slot-holding wrapper, never bare.
outcome: Bare runs bypassed the two-slot machine cap (REQ-126).

instruction: Run the RED case of every guard you write: a check that reads correctly can silently do nothing (e.g. a bash-4 builtin on a bash-3 host yields an empty array).
outcome: mapfile failed silently on bash 3.2.57, so the check kept passing a card that had two branches; caught only by running the RED case.

instruction: Never use `| grep -q` under pipefail; count with grep -c ... || true or redirect to /dev/null.
outcome: An early match closes the pipe, the writer takes SIGPIPE, and the if reads 141 as NO MATCH (L-25).

instruction: Refuse dispatch text that orders hand-driving a device (tap coordinates, UI dumps, pixel reads); detect the mechanism verbs but drop lines that prohibit them, so a correct dispatch is never refused.
outcome: Owner repeated the rule four times; the guard's first cut refused exactly the dispatch that named the verbs to forbid them ('a gate that can never pass gets routed around').

instruction: Resolve sibling scripts and tool homes from the script's own file location (BASH_SOURCE), never from $PWD or $(dirname $0) after a cd.
outcome: A branch adding a sibling script reported it MISSING from its own worktree (L-41).

instruction: Derive repo roots and session directories at run time; never hard-code one machine's absolute path.
outcome: A hard-coded home path made every ledger append fail with ENOENT on other hosts, silently, and the step-over check resolved nothing.

instruction: Before cutting a merge train, ask in seconds what the merge hook will say (door record for the tip, unticked verification boxes, coverage matrix, merge-tree conflict).
outcome: A train gated green for ten minutes was then refused by the hook on a coverage row and an unticked box, after the runner had already written MERGED ledger lines.

instruction: Pre-check each change against only the tests that can observe it (import closure) before it enters a shared batch; this filter can say 'broken', never 'safe'; exit 2 is never a verdict.
outcome: One card broke six tests and cost a full gate plus a full re-run to identify; 20 cards gated alone = 4 h vs 12 min shared.

instruction: Select inner-loop tests by reverse import closure from the changed files; the full suite runs only at the batch gate.
outcome: Whole-suite validation by every agent produced 16 queued waiters and host load 20.19; ~20 of ~3,182 tests could observe a typical change.
owner_words: you don't need additional pods, what you need is innovation

instruction: A full-suite run is the merge train's job, not a developer's; developers run targeted files.
outcome: With one pod of eleven agents both slots held full runs and sixteen agents queued computing the same ~3,182-test answer.

instruction: Cap heavy test runs machine-wide (two slots) with an atomic mkdir lock in a directory outside every worktree; release from EXIT/INT/TERM traps.
outcome: Four agents running suites at once drove load average to 137 (peak 189), starving emulators and timing out tools.

instruction: Count heavy runs by the real driver executables, excluding shells (and the scan itself) whose command line merely quotes the pattern; do not count narrow single-file runs.
outcome: Counting failed twice in opposite directions: worker count reported 4 for one legal run; quoted patterns counted a lock-wait loop as a run; four false alarms in one evening.

instruction: Measure gate numbers once with the tree sha and cite the output ('baseline <sha> (<date>)'); never hard-code counts in docs; report, don't judge; exit 2 only when a measurement could not be taken.
outcome: Two of four numbers in CLAUDE.md were stale on main (analyzer by 1, suite by 114), one line false for four days.

instruction: Distinguish 'could not run' (refusal, NOT MEASURED, rc 2) from pass/fail; a runner that silently skips missing inputs or reports SKIP as success reports a green it never measured.
outcome: A third test root was printed NOT MEASURED forever until a runner existed; missing toolchain must never read as green.

instruction: Write a DELIVERED status only through a per-sha health record proving the branch's own tests and gates are green in its own worktree.
outcome: Five of fourteen branches composed for a test window were red on their own tests or gates while carrying DELIVERED events.

instruction: A branch may only raise the test count; every ratchet baseline must be unchanged or tighter; compose all candidates into one tree and gate that.
outcome: A branch passed its own tests while breaking nine of another card's on the composed tree; per-branch gates cannot see interactions.

instruction: Every changed executable source line must be hit by a host test measured from coverage data; an unreachable line needs a waiver row naming why and the pin guarding it.
outcome: Owner directive #66 replaced the real-device merge condition with measured diff coverage plus simulation and mutation rows.

instruction: Commit a mutation battery per change; the runner exits 2 when any row got no verdict and refuses at every pre-row check (dirty tree, red unmutated pre-check, find count != 1).
outcome: A table that certifies a run that did not happen is worse than no table; batteries take a suite slot.

instruction: Generate candidate mutation rows by failure class from the diff; a surviving generated row fails the delivery unless replaced by an 'equivalent: <reason>' a certifier can verify.
outcome: Each class (cap bound, argument at every call site, ordering key, inverted guard, merge payload key, swallowed catch, wall clock) exists because a judge found it after delivery.

instruction: For every failure class the diff touches, the fix doc's coverage matrix must carry a row naming evidence; empty or short-reason cells are refused.
outcome: Every REWORK of one week was a reviewer finding one more untested class, one class per round; discovery was serial.

instruction: In a multi-card merge, attribute changed lines to cards at line level via commit subjects naming the card, not by file.
outcome: Two fix docs were failed for rows covering another card's lines; file-level ownership misattributed a shared file.

instruction: Keep verify scripts stdlib-only; a restricted parser errors on unsupported syntax, never guesses.
outcome: A pyyaml dependency dies on a clean checkout where CI installs no Python packages.

instruction: Run every committed script test file in CI so none is committed and run by nothing.
outcome: A node test was red on main because no CI stage ran it.

instruction: Ship every guard script with RED/GREEN cases that feed real inputs and assert deny/allow.
outcome: Guards are tested like product code; lock tests run in scratch slot dirs with bounded waits.

instruction: Every invariant id needs both a RED test case (a violating state) and a GREEN control; fail when one has none.
outcome: A WARN-only hard-delete rule never matched anything and shipped as a gate that could not fail (REQ-047); a GREEN control stops a predicate that flags everything (L-24).

instruction: Every probe fixture written by a harness in a typed language must compile.
outcome: Twice in one card an invalid fixture pinned the wrong behaviour: the generator was loosened to meet it and a guard went unpinned while its probe stayed green.

instruction: Tests must not share a constant database path across processes; point each test at a per-isolate temp directory.
outcome: Two concurrent test processes in one worktree opened and deleted the same file; failures landed in whichever suite was unlucky.

instruction: Force a race condition in a test; never rely on concurrent runs happening to collide.
outcome: A 5x concurrent run that happens to pass proves nothing about the shared-path hazard.

instruction: Introduce new checks as ratchets against a committed baseline when existing violations exist; a gate that cannot pass gets routed around.
outcome: 40 sites existed when the mktemp check landed; per-file baselines keep new files at zero.
enforcement: *_baseline files with --update in the same commit

instruction: Run inventory before invention: check the path, symbol, import, schema or similar code exists before creating or calling it; a miss is a hallucination class.
outcome: Hallucination classes H1-H4 named as defects, not style.

instruction: Generate fixtures, constants and spec values from their source by script with a --check drift mode; never copy values by hand.
outcome: Copying values by hand is how drift starts (L-10).

instruction: Keep one implementation of a shared check (e.g. the secret scanner) and call it everywhere; enforce that no copies exist.
outcome: Four copies of one grep matched SQL that clears a credential, failing every PR; fixing one copy broke the 'byte-identical' property (class C10).

instruction: A deploy config must parse and its target must equal what the app reads; a green command with no effect is worse than a red one.
outcome: A missing comma left ten indexes undeployable for over ten months, and the deploy target pointed at a database no app queried.

instruction: Read the toolchain's true version from its own metadata and check it against a committed record, never infer it from the install path.
outcome: An install directory named one version held another (D373).

instruction: Release artifacts are signed with the owner's key or not built; no debug-key fallback may be reachable from any build type.
outcome: A debug fallback shipped every production artifact debug-signed.

instruction: Prove a code marker is inside the built binary under every string encoding the runtime uses, and auto-detect the container for debug vs release builds.
outcome: An ASCII-only strings|grep returned 0 for a binary that contained the marker (UTF-16LE), and the check failed on the debug artifact every leg installed.

instruction: Run the cheapest smoke check on the exact binary before any expensive battery, record the binary hash and tree, and require positive post-conditions (prove the state was adopted, not 'not the login screen').
outcome: A ~200k-token battery plus an owner login round ran against a build that wedged on launch; a session plant that never landed still exited 0.
enforcement: smoke.sh writes .smoke_ok; run_battery.sh refuses without a matching md5

instruction: Accept a UI smoke criterion only as a named surface class or a resource id; a surface is usable only when its primary control is enabled, clickable, non-zero area and on screen.
outcome: A login screen with a present but dead button satisfied a free-text criterion and certified a wedged device.

instruction: Look at the app after every UI-touching merge with a visual check that can fail: rc-check every device command, validate counts as integers before comparing, and emit UNVERIFIED/NO-EVIDENCE rather than PASS on missing evidence.
outcome: The script could not fail (counted the wrong attribute; '0\n0' raised a syntax error and fell through to PASS); a restore path wedged at 0% shipped with 1,588 tests green.

instruction: Run the visual gate on every supported form factor, not just the one that never fails.
outcome: 17 overflow errors (worst 94 px) on phones; every train had only checked a tablet.

instruction: Split measurement from verdict (pure measurer + one decider) so the gate is testable off-device; keep each geometry rule disabled until measured.
outcome: Makes the visual gate testable on host fixtures (REQ-103).

instruction: Separate the evidence collector from the decider: a collector failure exits non-zero with no verdict; distinguish 'not captured' (null) from 'captured empty' ([]); an indeterminate verdict is reported, not an error.
outcome: A broken collector emitting a verdict reads as evidence; a toast alone must never name a cause.

instruction: Take a test verdict from the log AND the exit code; PASS requires at least one executed assertion; precondition failures report NOTRUN explicitly.
outcome: Four device legs printed 'Some tests failed' while the driver exited 0 and the runner wrote PASS.

instruction: Tick a verification box only by script from a result with PASS, a positive assertion count and an existing log naming the flow; write the evidence inline beside the tick.
outcome: The rig reported three flows PASS having executed zero assertions.

instruction: Turn unticked hardware-confirmation boxes into tracked debt (moved verbatim, not ticked, not deleted, recorded with a ledger event) and fail any card carrying debt without that event; never report it fully verified.
outcome: ~100 owed legs on two emulators at ~5 min each was a 4+ hour serial queue before any merge.

instruction: Run all committed end-to-end legs as one set against one prebuilt binary, and discover the set from the directory rather than a literal list.
outcome: 69 coded legs were never run as a set while 113 boxes waited; 411 lines of integration tests were run by nothing.

instruction: Map a change to the end-to-end tests that observe it by call graph; an all-match table (text or import closure) discriminates nothing and is not evidence.
outcome: Import closure matched 33 of 33 cards; the call graph matched 40 of 43 with median 9 legs, minimum 1 (not 32).

instruction: Device legs are code run by a runner, never hand-driven; a device leg does not take a test-suite slot and never wipes the session it relies on.
outcome: A pod waited for suite slots while both emulators sat idle.

instruction: Give exclusive access to a shared stateful test environment via a file lock: only the holder releases; stealing requires a stated reason.
outcome: Two batteries on the same emulators corrupt both results; a corrupted battery that reports numbers certifies falsely.

instruction: Prove a test environment's network actually resolves before reporting it booted; fakes at seams can hide a broken environment.
outcome: An emulator without a DNS override resolved no hostnames while legs faked the cloud at seams, hiding it for a day.

instruction: After every merge, build from main, install on every test device, and run the core business flows as an integration test with an exit code.
outcome: Prose checklists get skipped on the third tired round; hand-driving costs ~11 tool calls per device.
owner_words: after each merge build the latest apk from latest code and install on all 3 emulators, test one order scenario ... ensure both the flows are working as expected.

instruction: Run a deterministic multi-client simulation as a merge-gate step for any branch touching sync paths; re-baseline only in the same commit.
outcome: Owner #66: the simulation plus diff coverage replaces the real device as merge condition.

instruction: Prove a device test RED on host by replicating it (swap only the binding/factory); keep the replica in scratch, never commit a second copy.
outcome: Allows RED proof while the device rig is held; a committed replica would drift from the original.

instruction: A host fake of a hardware protocol answers only what the real device answers, including staying silent where the device is silent; record every received byte.
outcome: Answering a request the real unit ignores would let a wrong identification path compete.

instruction: Route every snapshot re-baseline through one checker that permits only the ruled delta.
outcome: Any other delta in a moved structure snapshot is a defect (D855/D856).

instruction: Prove RED first and paste it: revert the enabling hunk, show the test failing, restore, and record the hunk; 'green by construction' is not a RED proof.
outcome: Developer BINDING non-negotiable.

instruction: Mutation-prove the wiring, not the seam: a committed test must go RED when the production call site stops passing the argument.
outcome: Arguments collapsed at one call site while seam tests stayed green (class C2).

instruction: After every fix run the no-disturb net: analyzer counts that sum, every test root, and all repo gates, each with its exit code.
outcome: Developer BINDING.

instruction: State service invariants as runtime assertions, never comments (cent-precise money, no re-tender of a settled bill, correct-or-absent shared values, no swallowed send counted as success); grep sibling converters when fixing one.
outcome: Placeholder nulls/zeros read as fact by peers and swallowed sends (D-10).

instruction: Record every departure from the binding spec under a 'Deviations from the binding spec' heading; choosing a value from a prescribed range is a deviation.
outcome: Developer BINDING.

instruction: Measure a change to a signal channel in both directions: what stopped feeding it (per-producer worst-case silence before/after) and what started.
outcome: Developer BINDING.

instruction: A deviation defended by 'that case cannot exist' ships only with the falsifying fixture attempted and its output pasted; pin the call site and its owning file, not a declaration or a spelling.
outcome: An anti-gaming pin caught the literal '80mm' but passed the same attack written as '80'; second recurrence of the class.

instruction: When your diff renames or moves a source line, grep the committed mutation batteries for the old text before committing.
outcome: Battery find: strings name production source verbatim and go stale the moment a line is touched.

instruction: Run the committed probes first and touch them last; a wrong probe is reported, never rewritten by the certifier.
outcome: Test Agent BINDING.

instruction: Every battery and probe set carries an unmutated GREEN control; an all-RED table is a broken harness, not evidence.
outcome: Test Agent BINDING (L-24).
